### Stage 1 — Type a panel width (the stage that must land) — BUILT 2026-09-24

**As built.** Standard/braced slots have the width field windows already had, in the Selected Panel note. A commit sets `widthIn` and `lockedWidthIn` together and re-tiles that one wall through the anchor path; a per-panel **Reset to automatic** clears the pin and hands the width back to the tiler. The panel-boundary drag snaps the BOUNDARY to the eighth and derives both widths from it, so the pair total is conserved exactly. The arithmetic is a pure module, `packages/geometry/src/panelWidthEdit.ts` (+ its test file): `resolvePanelWidthEdit`, `resolvePanelBoundaryDrag`, `findSubMinimumPanelWidths`.

The 24in rider, exactly as specified: `fabricationMinPanelWidthIn` is a new `confirmed` `CatalogValue` in `data.ts` quoting Tommy verbatim with his axis; `panelWidthInRange.minIn` still reads 15.75 with its manufacturer note, and a test asserts it ("if this ever reads 24, a sourced number has been overwritten"); `PANEL_DRAG_FLOOR_IN`'s local `24` is deleted and both consumers read the catalog; `PANEL_DRAG_SNAP_TOLERANCE_IN = 2` is untouched. Typed entry **refuses** below the minimum (the field keeps focus and the text, states the limit, commits nothing) via a new `validate` prop on `LengthInput` — a refusal, deliberately not a clamp, sitting beside the existing clamp path rather than replacing it. **No other number in `data.ts` moved.**

**⚠ The plan was wrong about the entry point, and Stage 1 could not work without a fix.** It says "click a panel (existing `selectedSlot`), type into the width field." But clicking a panel's body runs the type cycle, and from a **standard** panel the first stop is a window; `handleToggleOpening` selects openings and braced panels and explicitly selects **nothing** when a slot lands back on "standard". So a standard panel could never BE the selected panel — the new field would have been unreachable for exactly the panels this stage is for. **Fix, kept as small as it could be: clicking a panel's width LABEL on the elevation selects it, without cycling anything.** That is the first half of what Tommy actually described ("click the numerical value of width of one panel and then... it opens up the number value so you can type in a new value"); the editing still happens in the note, so this is not the click-to-EDIT label the plan pushed to Stage 1b. A hand-set label draws bold, so a pin is visible on the drawing.

Two smaller notes: an edit that would move the wall's own total length is **refused whole** (guarded by a sum check after the re-tile) rather than partly applied; and the Review Log now carries one entry per panel below the minimum, however it got there, with the safety-gap board and the openings exempt for the reasons the plan gives.

**Written against the plan as it stood at commit `7c96b96`.** The plan moved while this was being built (`a656b7a`, `da3f09d`), and **Stage 0's and Stage 1's own text did not change** — what changed sits around them: the tiler's `absorb` decision, the sill's move to 24in, the Standard-width clamp and the hyphen drop are now **Stage 1r**, a separate gate commit that lands before Tommy draws. None of them is done here, deliberately. The one place the newer text touches what this pass wrote: the sub-minimum Review Log entries will mostly stop firing once absorb lands, leaving the three residual cases absorb cannot reach — which is exactly what that entry is for.

**Evidence beyond the unit tests:** `apps/web/harness/smearforn-stage-0-1/` — a CDP harness IN THE REPO, with screenshots and an `evidence.json`. It shows a new project offering the Wall tab only, `41 1/2` committing as `41½`, `20` refused with the limit stated and the draft kept, per-panel reset returning a panel to 40in, a fractional-pixel drag committing 44½"/35½" with the run total conserved, a drag past the floor stopping at 24in — and **all eleven Rogers-Sehorn ADU widths typed in sequence with none refused.**

Tommy: *"We need a way to manipulate the widths of individual panels. Maybe when you are on the edit tool and click the numerical value of width of one panel and then click/highlight one of the edges, it opens up the number value so you can type in a new value. And/or also a tool should allow the user to click and drag a wall to shrink one and grow another."*

**The second interaction already exists** — the panel-boundary drag does exactly "shrink one and grow another", conserving the pair total, with the 24in floor and the role-handoff Tommy specified (`WallElevationDiagram.tsx:874-938`). What it lacks is the eighth snap (above). **The first interaction does not exist for standard panels** — only for windows, which already have a `LengthInput` width field in the Selected Panel note (`page.tsx:7062-7074`).

**So Stage 1 is: give standard/braced slots the width field windows already have.**

- **Entry point.** Click a panel (existing `selectedSlot`), type into the width field in the Selected Panel note. Tommy's phrasing suggests clicking the number on the elevation itself; a click-to-edit label on the diagram is a nicer gesture and a bigger change. **Recommendation: the Selected Panel note this pass**, because it reuses a field that already parses fractions, already clamps, already shows a clamp notice, and already relocates the selection after a retile. The on-diagram editor is a Stage-1b nicety if there is time.
- **Committing sets `widthIn` AND `lockedWidthIn` together**, exactly as the drag already does (`page.tsx:2085-2087`), then re-tiles that one wall through the anchor path.
- **Where the width comes from.** The typed panel grows; the *free* run shrinks. Concretely: the pinned width is reserved out of the budget and the unpinned standard/braced slots re-tile into what is left, which may change their count. The wall's total length never moves.
- **Constraints, and what happens when an edit is impossible:**
  - **The wall's total length is fixed.** Always. It is not a thing a panel width edit may change.
  - **Maximum: `panelWidthInRange.maxIn` = 48in** (confirmed). Above it, clamp and say so — the existing clamp-notice pattern.
  - **Minimum: REFUSE at 24in**, the new `confirmed` Building Integrity fabrication minimum. The field keeps focus, states the limit, and does not commit. Not a warning — a panel the shop cannot build is not a thing to negotiate at the keyboard. See "The minimum panel width" above for how it is recorded and why `panelWidthInRange.minIn` is untouched.
  - **The same constant drives the drag floor.** `PANEL_DRAG_FLOOR_IN`'s local `24` is deleted and both consumers read the catalog value. The ±2" snap tolerance and the role-handoff are unchanged ergonomics.
  - **Auto-generated panels below the minimum are reported, not refused** — the tiler can already produce them (see the defect above) and refusing at the tiler would change every existing wall. Review Log only, this pass.
  - **No room left.** If the free run cannot give up the width — every other slot on the wall is pinned, an opening, or a corner — **refuse the commit**, keep focus, and say how much is actually available. Never partially apply, never silently shrink a corner panel.
- **Reset control** beside the field: clears `lockedWidthIn`, wall re-tiles, panel returns to automatic.

**ADU reach after Stage 1:** every panel width in the schedule is typeable — 43", 41½", 37½", 35", 31½", 30", 29½", 28½", 25½", 24" — and **none of them trips any limit the app enforces**, so no warning fires anywhere in this job. Any wall whose panel *count* the tiler happens to produce correctly is fully reproducible. **Not** reachable: walls needing more or fewer panels than the tiler makes, the triple headers, the wall that stops short.

---

### Stage 1x — the locked-width refusal: a pin the wall cannot honour — BUILT 2026-09-30

**As built.** A hand-set (`lockedWidthIn`) width is still re-forced after every re-tile, but the re-force is now **paid for exactly or refused outright**. The arithmetic is a new pure module, `packages/geometry/src/lockedWidthReforce.ts` (+ its test file): `planLockedWidthReforce` (apply or refuse, the pinned set planned **jointly**, all-or-nothing per pin — see the joint-planning section below, which is load-bearing), `honourableLockedWidthRangeIn` (the widest and narrowest hand-set width a wall will take on that slot right now, clamped to catalog limits passed IN), and `findUnhonouredLockedWidths` (every dormant pin in a building, for reporting). `reconcileBracedPlacement`'s own signature is **unchanged** — it has 7+ call sites and no business composing English — and its last statement is now `return planLockedWidthReforce(result).slots`. `shedWidthToNearestUnlocked` is gone. `settleResidualEighths` moved out of `bracedPlacement.ts` into its own module (a verbatim move, plus its first direct tests) so the two refusals share one settling discipline instead of having two; the corner-brace combine still calls it.

**The defect, re-measured here before any code was written** (the Open Items bullet's own fixture: every eighth 150in–400in, standard widths {40, 48}, two corners, one 61.5in window against the corner, a lock of 24in or 48in on the first standard-family slot, skipping walls the tiler itself does not sum): **8,004 cases, 362 off their own length, from 23⅞in SHORT to 11¼in long, and 2 carrying a 0in panel.** The named case reproduces exactly — a 150in two-corner wall, lock 48in → 161¼in, lock 24in → 137¼in. On that wall the whole run is `corner 25.5 | window 61.5 | gap 0.75 | standard 36.75 | corner 25.5`: **one** standard-family slot, and it is the pinned one, so the old shed had nowhere to put the delta and did nothing at all.

**TOMMY'S DECISION, 2026-09-29, implemented verbatim:** *a locked/dragged width the wall length cannot honour is* **refused outright** *— nothing changes, and the message names what is in the way and the widest legal value. The wall's real length is never violated.*

#### Which gesture is refused — and the answer is "the re-force", not the user's last click

**The width EDIT was already guarded and needed nothing.** `resolvePanelWidthEdit`'s `refuse-no-room` plus `retileWallAroundPins`' two guards (the wall must still sum; the pin must come back at exactly its pinned width) mean a typed width never commits a broken wall. Verified on the named case: typing 48in on that 150in wall is refused today, because the wall has no free panel to take the 11¼in from.

**What reached the broken path was a pin that was LEGAL when it was set** and became unpayable because of a later, unrelated edit — the wall dragged shorter, an opening added, a run stop, a different standard width. Refusing *that* gesture would refuse an edit the user did not just make, and would let a panel pin block a wall drag (which is the third queued refusal's territory, not this one's). So the thing refused is the **re-force**: the slot keeps the width the tiler gave it, the wall's length is exact, nothing else on the wall moves, and **`lockedWidthIn` is never cleared** — the pin is dormant, not destroyed, and reapplies by itself the moment the wall can afford it again.

Two surfaces say so, sharing one set of words (`apps/web/app/lockedWidthNotices.ts` + its test file, the `runStopNotices.ts` pattern — numbers testable without a browser, wording testable without a tiler):

1. **The Selected Panel note**, which until now said a hand-set width *"survives a re-tile of this wall"* unconditionally. On these walls that was simply untrue. It now reads, for example: *"Hand-set at 48", but NOT in force on this wall: every other panel on this wall is an opening, a corner, a Safety/Gap spacer or hand-set itself, so there is no panel left to take the 11¼" from. This panel is built at 36¾", the width the tiler gives it, so the wall's own length stays exact. The only width this panel can have right now is 36¾". Nothing was changed to make it fit: drag this wall longer or remove the opening on it, and this width comes back by itself."*

   ⚠ **The recovery advice is composed per wall, not a constant, and it used to over-promise three different ways on this very wall.** "Reset another panel to automatic" is offered only when there IS another hand-set panel (on this wall `freePanelCount` is 0 precisely because there is not); "remove an opening" only when the wall has one AND the pin needs length; and "lengthen the wall" only for a pin WIDER than the tiler’s width — for a pin that is narrower the problem is the opposite one, nowhere to put the surplus, and at a 48in standard width lengthening creates no absorb headroom at all because the tiler refills to the ceiling. That case now asks for a **shorter** wall. The three new counts on `LockedWidthRefusal` exist for exactly this.
2. **The Review Log**, one entry per dormant pin, the `findCornerBraceCombineRefusals` shape and for the same reason: the wall is legal, which is exactly why nobody would otherwise see that **the panel is fabricated at the tiler's width and not at the one somebody typed**. It names the wall, the slot and the story inside the note, because the dedupe keys on `note` alone and two symmetric walls would otherwise collapse to one entry.

#### ⚠ One thing it changes about the shipped width-edit gesture, and the numbers for it

Because the re-force can now refuse, `retileWallAroundPins`' pin check **fires in cases where it previously could not**: a width that the wall could only honour by pushing a neighbour below the 24in fabrication minimum or past the 48in catalog maximum used to commit, with the unbuildable neighbour reported after the fact by `findSubMinimumPanelWidths` (or, past the maximum, **not reported at all**). It is refused now, with its own sentence — *"Refused: 48" is not a width this wall can hold — it needs 11" from the rest of the wall, and the 1 automatic panel here can only give up 8" before it drops below the 24" fabrication minimum. The widest this panel can be hand-set to right now is 45", and the narrowest is 24". Nothing was changed."* — rather than the generic *"couldn't be applied without moving this wall's own total length"*, which was not true of it.

**This makes the two width-edit paths agree.** `redistributeFreeRun`, the path a hand-edited wall already takes, has always refused exactly these cases (see `narrowestAcceptablePinWidthIn`'s own note: on a 16–28ft wall with a panel deleted the narrowest pin the wall will take is 44½in). Until now the same edit was refused on a hand-edited wall and committed with an unbuildable panel on a tiler-laid one.

**Measured, so the cost is visible rather than asserted.** Typing each of eleven Rogers-Sehorn ADU widths (43, 41½, 37½, 35, 31½, 30, 29½, 28½, 48, 24, 40) on the middle panel of every wall from 8ft to 48ft:

* **at the 40in default standard width: 25 of 451 refused**, and all 25 are walls of **12ft or less**, whose free run is one to three panels. Nothing at 13ft or above refuses.
* **at a 48in standard width: 168 of 451 refused.** That is not this change misbehaving — it is what a 48in standard width means: the tiler fills the wall with panels at or just under the 48in ceiling, so there is no headroom to hand a surplus back to, and any pin narrower than the tiler's own width has nowhere to put the difference. Sweeping every eighth from 240in to 600in at that standard width, a 24in pin is refused on **47.7%** of walls. The old behaviour in those cases was a single neighbour grown past 48in.

⚠ **THE OTHER COLUMN, which the first write-up of this section left out, and it reverses the reading.** A refusal rate is only a cost if what it replaces was acceptable. It was not:

| standard width | refused now | **what those refusals replace** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 40in (the default) | 25 of 451 | **162 of 451 commits that produced an unbuildable panel** |
| 48in | 47.7% of walls | **86.7% of walls silently committing a panel past the 48in manufacturer maximum, reported nowhere** |

`findSubMinimumPanelWidths` only ever looked at the *minimum*, so a panel grown past the 48in maximum was reported by nothing at all and reached the cut list, the fabrication sheet and the shop drawing at a width no supplier makes. **The refusal is the smaller half of this change, not its cost**, and the 47.7% figure read on its own understates the case badly.

**Practical exposure at the shipped default is 25 of 451, all on walls of 12ft or less.** Nothing in this spec, the Rogers-Sehorn material or any of the six harnesses uses a 48in standard width — the ADU's irregular widths are hand-set on a **40in** project.

⚠ **The real fix for that case is bigger than this change and is not attempted here:** `retileWallAroundPins` never tells the tiler about the pin, so the tiler cannot do the obvious thing and emit **one more, narrower free panel** (budget 481¼in → 11 panels at 43¾in instead of 11 at 47⅝in plus a 52¼in). Teaching the tiler about pins changes the panel COUNT on a pinned wall, which is what `tilerWouldChangeThePanelCount` exists to catch and what the slot-index pinning rule forbids outright. **His call, and recorded as an Open Item rather than guessed at.**

#### Three things it deliberately does not do

1. **It never clears a refused pin.** ⚠ **This is in tension with one line of the Stage 1 design note above**, which said unfittable pins "are **released** — their `lockedWidthIn` is cleared". That line predates Tommy's decision, whose words are *"nothing changes"*; retaining the pin is what "nothing changes" means, and clearing it would be a silent deletion of a hand edit on a feature whose entire point is that a typed width survives. **If he wants the pin released instead, that is a one-line change and his call to make.**
2. **It never swallows or adds a panel.** `planCornerBraceCombine` may remove one, because a combined slot physically IS one panel where two stood; a width pin is not, and a wall that quietly lost or gained a panel because of a pin would be a second silent change made in the name of preventing one.
3. **It never polices the pinned value itself.** A stored file carrying a 20in or 60in pin is honoured if the run can pay for it, exactly as before — limits bind at the point of EDIT, never at load.

#### ⚠ The pinned set is planned JOINTLY — and this is load-bearing for the editing model, not a refinement

**The first version of this refusal paid for each pin out of the FREE run only** (`freeRunCandidates`, which by construction excludes every other pinned slot), one pin at a time, repeating to a fixpoint. That is wrong, and wrong in the one direction this feature exists to prevent: **it silently discarded hand-set widths that `main` honoured correctly.** Caught in review before merge; fixed in the same function.

The case that makes it a defect rather than a conservatism — a 9ft two-corner wall after one elevation boundary drag:

```
corner 25.5 | standard 28.5 (pinned 24) | standard 28.5 (pinned 33) | corner 25.5
```

**24 + 33 = 57, and the pair already holds 28.5 + 28.5 = 57.** Both pins are payable with *zero* net change anywhere else — and per-pin planning refused both, because neither is payable on its own and the run has no free panel. The repeat-to-fixpoint walk could not help: no pass applied anything, so it exited on the first iteration.

**That shape is what the shipped gestures produce, not a contrivance.**

* `handleDragResizePanels` — the elevation boundary drag — writes `widthIn` **and** `lockedWidthIn` on **both** halves of the pair it moves, to two different widths whose sum is exactly what the pair already held. So it creates a residual-cancelling pair on **every single use**.
* `retile.ts`'s preserving path re-reconciles **every** wall against its stored slots, so dragging any other wall, editing the footprint or changing a run stop re-forces the pins on this one. Measured end to end on a 211in wall at the 40in default — two typed widths (43", 41½") and one boundary drag to the 24" floor leave `[25.5, 43, 41.5, 30, 0.75, 44.75, 25.5]`, 211in exactly, 4 pins, all inside [24, 48]. After **one unrelated retile**: per-pin planning returned `[25.5, 40, 39.625, 39.625, 0.75, 40, 25.5]` with all four pins dormant; `main` and the shipped joint planner both return the wall unchanged.
* ⚠ **And Tommy decided on 2026-09-30 that the app will tile only on the FIRST draw**, with everything after it direct manipulation — panels enter and grow with a wall drag, and the boundary drag pins exactly two panels. Under that model **an ordinary wall has every standard-family slot pinned**, which is precisely the shape per-pin planning refused wholesale. **Joint pin planning is a prerequisite for the editing model he has chosen**, and is written here as load-bearing rather than as an edge case that was patched.

**How it works now.** The outstanding pins are planned as a group: their **aggregate** residual is settled across the free run in one `settleResidualEighths` call, so pins that cancel cost nothing and a pinned set that already accounts for the wall's budget needs no free panel at all (the settle of a zero residual succeeds over an empty candidate list, which is exactly right). `planCornerBraceCombine`'s plan-then-commit is the precedent.

**All-or-nothing is kept, and it is still per pin.** When the aggregate cannot be settled the group gives up exactly one pin at a time — the one pulling hardest in the direction the aggregate is already too far, the LATER slot of a tie, so the earlier slot keeps its width — and tries again. A pin is therefore either in force at its own exact width or refused whole; nothing is partially applied and **no pin is ever cleared on any path**. Dropping the biggest offender rather than simply the last pin is deliberate: with residuals of 9in and 2in and 4in of headroom, dropping the 2in leaves the 9in still unpayable and loses both, where dropping the 9in pays the 2in.

**The walk still repeats until a pass applies nothing**, which is what makes the function a FIXPOINT — a hard requirement, since `retile.ts` runs it over every wall on any edit anywhere in the building, and a refused pin that became payable on a second pass would move a wall with no user action at all. That is the same defect the corner-brace combine was fixed for on 2026-09-29.

**Measured, three ways.** (1) **Never worse, often better:** on 300,000 random pinned runs the joint planner honours **at least as many pins as the per-pin one on every single case (0 worse)** and strictly more on 3,181. (2) **400,000 adversarial cases** — off-grid pins, pins outside [24, 48], pins on corner/window/door/column/safety-gap slots, zero-width slots, 1–8 slots: total conserved in eighths on all 400,000, idempotent on the second *and* third pass on all 400,000, no pin ever cleared or created, input never mutated, no throw, no hang, 942,762 pins set with 224,680 honoured and 718,082 refused so non-vacuous. (3) **The new sweep row below.**

**It also fixes a second symptom of the same root cause.** `resolvePanelWidthEdit` deliberately allows a zero-delta edit on a wall with no free slot — "lock this panel at what it already is". Per-pin planning refused the whole all-pinned set, so `retileWallAroundPins`' pin guard fired and the edit was refused where `main` committed it; worse, the sentence was then composed against a FRESH tiling rather than the current wall, so `legalWidthClause` would say *"The only width this panel can have right now is 40""* about a panel sitting at 37¼" on a wall that adds up. Joint planning makes the all-pinned set payable, so neither the refusal nor the false sentence arises.

#### The sweep

`packages/geometry/src/lockedWidthReforce.test.ts` runs the whole path a real wall takes — tile, brace, pin, re-tile, reconcile — over **684,588 cases in ~9s**: every eighth of wall length from 100in to 400in × standard widths {40, 48} × 4 corner configs × 2 gap ends × 3 opening sets × 2 lock values {24in, 48in} × 3 pin placements (first standard-family slot, last, both). Five properties per case: the total never moves (**asserted against the wall's own real length on all 684,588**, not just against the tiler's total), no 0in panel, no panel pushed outside [24in, 48in] that the brace pass had not already left there, **all-or-nothing per pin** (each pin is either in force or reported refused at exactly the width its slot kept — nothing in between, and no pin cleared), and idempotence. **889,606 pins set: 605,669 honoured, 283,937 refused.** A second, coarser sweep covers the reachable route — the pin came from a LONGER version of the wall, i.e. the wall was dragged shorter under it — over 3,228 cases, 727 of them refusing.

⚠ **A SECOND SWEEP ROW, added because the first one could not see the regression above.** `PLACEMENTS`' `both` sets **the same** lock value on the first and last standard-family slot, so 684,588 cases never once constructed a **residual-cancelling pair** — two pins set to DIFFERENT widths that sum to what the pair already holds, which is what the boundary drag produces on every use. All-or-nothing and no-pin-cleared both passed happily while both pins were thrown away. The new row builds that pair across the same grid (first and last standard-family slot, one half wider by 4½in or 12in and the other narrower by the same, skipping any case where a half would land outside [24in, 48in]) and asserts the four properties above **plus the one they cannot express: the pair is HONOURED.** **60,777 cases, 0 violations. 7,296 of those pairs have no automatic panel on the run at all** — payable only because the residuals cancel — and run against the per-pin planner this row reported **7,296 violations, every one a "2 of 2 pins refused" on exactly those 7,296 pairs.** So the row is not merely red before the fix: the regression and the no-free-panel pairs are the same set, which is what says the diagnosis is the right one.

**What the sweep deliberately does NOT cover**, so "not covered" stays distinguishable from "covered and passing": the tiler's own opening-overflow (swept, but the invariant is then asserted against the tiler's own total rather than the wall's length — that defect is its own Open Item and is not blamed on this code); walls under 100in and over 400in (the pin arithmetic has no length term, and the braced product sweep already covers 12in–600in underneath it); pins outside [24in, 48in] and pins on non-standard slots (unit-tested instead); the 39in Square Bale standard width (dropped for runtime); and second stories, zones, mid-wall beams, headers and run stops, none of which changes a slot's width.

**Evidence in a browser.** Two new steps in `apps/web/harness/smearforn-stage-0-1/`.

**Step 12 — the refusal.** Pins panels at 48in one after another on a 4-panel wall until the automatic run cannot pay for one. The third is refused whole; **the wall's own total is identical after every attempt**, no panel ends outside [24in, 48in], and the two pins before it are still honoured — because a refusal that refuses everything is not what was asked for.

⚠ **It is red on `main` @ `f100bd3` — but not for the reason first written here, and the real reason is the better story.** The claim was that the old shed drove neighbours to 16in, then 6in, then clamped one at 0in, "with the wall's own total moving every time", and that `totalNeverMoved` is the check that catches it. **That does not reproduce.** `main` records `totals: [160,160,160,160,160]` and **`totalNeverMoved: true`**; the check that fails is **`narrowestAfter >= FABRICATION_MIN_IN`**. `shedWidthToNearestUnlocked` hands the whole delta to one neighbour with `Math.max(0, widthIn + deltaIn)` and no lower bound but zero, so the wall still sums — it just sums with a panel no shop can build, and `retileWallAroundPins`' "the wall must still sum" guard waves it through. Re-measured here against `main`'s own `bracedPlacement.ts`, on a 160in four-panel wall at the 40in standard width with two corners: the first pin commits a **20¼in** panel, the second a **12¼in** one, both silently; the third is the only attempt that moves the total (160in → 195¾in) and is therefore the only one `main` **already** refuses. **The 0in clamp is unreachable on a four-panel wall** — `Math.max(0, …)` only bites when the chosen neighbour is narrower than the delta — and the no-free-slot case this refusal was really built for makes the shed a complete **no-op** instead, which is the shape that moves the wall's length by the whole delta (the named 150in wall; 362 of 8,004 fixture walls). A mechanism claim that does not reproduce undermines evidence that is otherwise solid, so it is corrected here, in the harness README and in `run.mjs` rather than quietly left.

**Step 12b — the residual-cancelling pair, end to end.** Drags **every** boundary on a run, which pins every panel on it (the drag writes `lockedWidthIn` on both halves of each pair it moves), then takes **one unrelated retile from a different wall** via a run-stop change — `retileAllForRunStops` re-reconciles every wall in the building against its own stored slots, which is the real path by which an edit anywhere re-forces the pins everywhere. It asserts that every hand-set width is still there afterwards, that it is still there after a **second** retile, that the wall's own total never moved, and that nothing ended outside [24in, 48in]. ⚠ **`automaticPanelsLeft === 0` is a load-bearing fixture check:** with one automatic panel left the pair can lean on it and the broken per-pin planner passes too. **This step was red on this branch's own first commit and is green on `main`**, which is the point — the refusal must not cost hand edits the code it replaced kept.

**Flags check for this pass (6 points), re-run after the joint-planning fix.** 1. **No building value moved** — `fabricationMinPanelWidthIn` (24in), `panelWidthInRange` (15.75–48in), `cornerPanelWidthIn`, `SAFETY_GAP_WIDTH_IN`, the standard widths and the `max ≥ 2 × min` coupling are all untouched; `data.ts` has no diff at all, and neither does `packages/panel-catalog` or `packages/calc-engine`. 2. **No new building value invented** — the settle uses the tiler's own `TILER_MIN/MAX_PANEL_WIDTH_IN`, and every number a user SEES is passed in from the catalog, the `panelWidthEdit.ts` convention. The three counts added to `LockedWidthRefusal` (`bracedFreePanelCount`, `otherPinnedPanelCount`, `openingCount`) are counts of the wall's own slots, not quantities. 3. **Nothing provisional presented as settled** — the Review Log entry carries `pending-BI-confirmation`, and the reason is stated in the code: the vocabulary has two values and `confirmed` would be a lie, because nobody has confirmed which width was meant. ⚠ **And a braced panel is now named as a braced panel:** `isFreePanel` includes `"braced"` (as `shedWidthToNearestUnlocked` did, and as `planCornerBraceCombine` does), so paying for a pin can change a braced panel's width, and braced placement derives from `seismicBracedPanelSpacingFt` and the braced-wall-line figure — **neither confirmed**. The Review Log note says so where it previously did not. 4. **No gap papered over** — the std-48 refusal rate **and the column it replaces**, the "tiler is never told about the pin" limitation, the release-vs-retain tension, the corrected red-on-`main` mechanism, and the one braced-panel case still NOT reported (below) are all written up rather than smoothed out. 5. **Every claim measured** — every figure in this section was produced by this branch's own tests, including the corrected `main` mechanism, which was re-measured against `main`'s own `bracedPlacement.ts` rather than quoted. 6. **Everything deliberately unfixed is written up** — the items in point 4, the decision not to touch the corner-brace combine or `settleResidualEighths`' behaviour, and:

⚠ **One thing is deliberately NOT reported, and it is a real gap.** The Review Log names a braced panel only on a **refused** pin, in the future tense ("if this wall gets the room back, the panel that would pay is a braced one"). The case where a braced panel **has actually been resized** to pay for an honoured pin produces no Review Log entry at all, because an honoured pin produces none. Closing that needs `planLockedWidthReforce` to report which slots its settle moved and a new entry in `page.tsx` to carry it — a **new reported fact**, not a sentence, and out of scope for a correctness fix. It is not a regression: it is the same silence `shedWidthToNearestUnlocked` kept, and the corner-brace combine's own entry covers the brace-placement half of it.

* **`npx vitest run`: 138 files / 2710 tests, all passing.** The branch before the joint-planning fix was 138 / 2692, so **+18 tests and no new file**: 6 joint-planning unit tests and the residual-cancelling-pair sweep row in `lockedWidthReforce.test.ts`, and 11 in `lockedWidthNotices.test.ts` (the narrowed recovery advice, the braced-payer clause, and `lockedWidthEditRefusalSentence`, **which had no test at all** although it is exported, wired into `handleSetPanelWidth` and quoted verbatim in two documents). `require.resolve('@building-integrity/geometry')` was confirmed to point at this worktree's own `packages/geometry/src/index.ts` before any of those numbers were trusted.

What actually moved it is **47 insertions and 4 deletions in `bracedPlacement.test.ts` itself**, at its own lines 472 and 528 — i.e. a block **added above it in the same file**, net +43, which is exactly 727 − 684. ### Stage 1r — the gate: absorb, the 24in minimums, the hyphen — BUILT 2026-09-25

**As built, on branch `smearforn-stage-1r`, in four commits.**

**Absorb.** `computePlainSizing` splits a leftover two ways only when the parts total ≥ 48in, and otherwise emits ONE panel of `standardWidth + remainder`. `buildEvenMiddle` (the ≤12ft no-gap path, which the plan named and which turned out to need it just as badly — a 40⅛in budget at a 40in standard gave two ~20in panels) now floors its count at `floor(budget ÷ 24in)` as well as capping it at `ceil(budget ÷ standardWidth)`. The tie at exactly 48in goes to the split, asserted. `computeSillRunWidths` is deliberately untouched — see the gap noted below.

**The proof is preserved as a test, in two places.** `data.test.ts` asserts `panelWidthInRange.maxIn >= 2 * fabricationMinPanelWidthIn.value` directly, plus a sweep naming the first untileable band if it ever stops holding; `tilerFabricationLimits.test.ts` (in `apps/web`, the only place that imports both packages) asserts the tiler's own duplicated copies of those two numbers still agree with the catalog, because `packages/geometry` deliberately has no dependency on `packages/panel-catalog` and a duplicated number defended only by a comment is a number that drifts.

**Sweeps.** No tiler-generated panel under 24in or over 48in, and the wall total conserved exactly as integer eighths, over every eighth from 96in to 720in × `standardWidthIn ∈ {24, 39, 40, 48}` × both gap ends × all four corner combinations, plain and with 1–3 openings; plus a whole-footprint sweep over every rectangular ADU from 16×16ft to 44×44ft at every whole foot.

**The three residuals each got a test saying they are deliberately unfixed**, so "not attempted" stays distinguishable from "still broken". The 51–75in two-corner band is untouched, per Tommy's deferral to corner geometry after admin tooling. *(Record of Stage 1r as it shipped. **The band was fixed on 2026-09-25** — corner absorb — and its residual test now asserts the fix instead; see Open Items.)*

**The safety-gap combine, measured rather than assumed.** `applyBracedPlacement`'s corner-brace combine can still shed a panel out of range — and it is **pre-existing**: over the same sweep, 32,266 cases produced an out-of-range panel before absorb and 3,279 after, and 3,279 is exactly the number of cases where the combine fires, either side of the change. So absorb removes nine tenths of them and creates none. Left unfixed (it is braced placement, not the tiler) with a test pinning the behaviour. **⚠ Superseded 2026-09-29 — the combine IS fixed now**, and the test that pinned the broken behaviour is rewritten to assert the fix instead; the measurement above still stands as the reason the tiler side is trusted, but its last sentence no longer describes the code. See the struck-through entry under "Still open" for what replaced it.

**Sills.** `sillMinWidthIn` is now a `CatalogValue<number>` at 24, `confirmed`, with the manufacturer's 600mm/23.622in figure and its provenance preserved *inside* the note. It reaches the Review Log through a new `CATALOG_SUPERSESSIONS` list appended **after** `toReviewLog` rather than mislabelled as pending — the value really is confirmed, and `toReviewLog` correctly filters confirmed entries out. **No other catalog number moved:** the whole `data.ts` diff is that one value plus doc comments.

**The hyphen.** `panelInstances.ts:282` emits `${direction}${n}`. `combinedPanelLabel` no longer parses: `PanelInstance` now carries `direction` and `panelNumber` as real fields, and the combined label is `N3+4+5`. Two tests, one named for the exact `N4-undefined+undefined` rendering and written as a property over the real generator's output. **Audit result: that was the only parse in the repo.** The only *format* that still adds a hyphen to a name is the jack-stud shipping ref `${inst.name}-JS1`, which nothing parses and which is now less ambiguous than the old `N-4-JS1`; the OBJ exporter's `g ${panel.label}_${memberId}` uses an underscore. Everything else keys or renders the name.

**The Standard width setting is clamped to [24, 48]** and its title no longer advertises the manufacturer's 15¾in floor. This matters more than it looks: absorb only ever resolves the *leftover*, so a standard width below the fabrication floor makes every full-width panel on every wall unbuildable and no amount of absorbing fixes it. There is a test named for exactly that.

**Two things the plan did not say, found while building it:**

- **`buildEvenMiddle` needed absorb as much as `computePlainSizing` did**, and the plan's framing ("the two-way split") only describes the latter. The ≤12ft path reaches the same failure through `Math.ceil`.
- **The grid sweep's "no standard slot exceeds `standardWidthIn`" rule had to be restated, not just relaxed.** Absorb makes oversized panels legal on purpose — unbuildable is worse than oversized, so the floor outranks the cap — and what survives is the ceiling, which is the bound that actually protects a cut list. Restated with a comment saying why, in the shape Stage 2 will need again for pinned slots.

**A gap this change creates and does not close:** `sillMinWidthIn` is now a confirmed 24in that **nothing enforces and nothing reports**. `computeSillRunWidths` can still emit a 22in sill, and `findSubMinimumPanelWidths` walks wall *slots*, which a sill is not. The plan scoped 1r's tiler work to `computePlainSizing` and `buildEvenMiddle` only, so this was left alone deliberately — but a confirmed limit with no consumer looks from the outside exactly like one being honoured, so it is written into the function's own doc comment and belongs in Open Items.

**Verified, not merely merged**, per the gate rule: `npx vitest run` green (111 files, 2040 tests), `tsc --noEmit` clean on a cleared `.next`, and the browser harness re-run against the real app — 12 of 12 checks, including all eleven ADU widths typed with none refused, and a new step that walks the viewer dial through all four wall elevations of a drawn footprint and finds nothing under 24in on any of them.

### Stage 2 — Insert, replace and delete a panel — BUILT 2026-09-25

**As built, on branch `smearforn-stage-2`, in five commits.**

**The tool.** A "Place a panel" group in the wall-elevation left bar: the nine click-cycle stops (Standard, four braced styles, Window, Door, Column, Big Header) plus **Delete**, each a toggle. With one armed, a click on a panel's body **replaces** it (or deletes it) instead of cycling it, and every legal boundary on the row becomes a drawn, dashed, clickable **insert** target. The panel-boundary drag stands down while the tool is armed — one strip cannot mean two things — and the width label stops swallowing clicks, or the panel under it would be the one spot the tool could not reach. Corner and safety-gap refuse, in words, on both replace and delete.

**The arithmetic is a pure module**, `packages/geometry/src/panelPlacement.ts` (+ its test file), the same shape Stage 1 took: `resolvePanelInsert`, `resolvePanelReplace`, `resolvePanelDelete`, `redistributeFreeRun`, `insertableBoundaryRange`, `shiftSlotCoverage`, and `PLACEABLE_PANEL_TYPES` — which a test asserts against `nextPanelCycleState`'s own reachable roster, so the two cannot drift apart. The catalog minimum/maximum are passed in, not imported, for the reason `panelWidthEdit.ts` already gives.

**⚠ The plan said "both use the existing anchor mechanism", and that turned out not to be buildable as written — this is the one place the build departs from the plan, deliberately.** `retileWithOpenings` derives the free run's COUNT from the budget alone, so it answers "how many panels does this wall hold" identically every time it is asked. Re-deriving the count is exactly what an insert or a delete must not do: a wall that just gained a hand-placed panel loses it again on the way back out, and a delete of an automatic panel is a no-op because the budget did not change. So the count is carried by **the slot array itself** — already persisted, no new key, **no `PROJECT_FILE_VERSION` bump** — and only the free run's *widths* are recomputed:

- Let `B` be what is left for the free run (the wall total minus every fixed width: corners, the gap, every opening, every pin) and `n` the free slots the edit left standing. The run keeps `n` when it legally can: `n' = min(max(n, ceil(B / 48in)), floor(B / 24in))`. `distributeEighths` then makes every part `floor(B/n')` or `ceil(B/n')`, so **both fabrication bounds hold for every panel rather than on average**.
- **The count may shrink, never grow.** Growing it would answer "I want one fewer panel" by inventing one, so that case is refused and said out loud.
- `0 < B < 24in` is **refused**, not rounded away — a sliver has no legal home and nothing to absorb into without moving a corner or an opening, which this module never does. `B === 0` exactly is fine: the free run simply ends up empty.

**The rider that makes Stage 1 and Stage 2 compose, and it is not optional.** `retileWallAroundPins` falls back to `redistributeFreeRun` whenever the tiler's answer **disagrees with the wall about how many standard-family slots it has, in either direction**. Without it the next width edit silently re-tiles the hand edit away — and the wall still sums to its own length while doing it, so neither of that function's existing guards notices. That is the silent revert this plan forbids, and `apps/web/app/handPlacedWallRetile.{ts,test.ts}` pins it through the real tiler in both directions. A wall that has never been hand-placed on gives the same count both ways and takes the tiler path exactly as before.

**⚠ "In either direction" is a review fix, and the one-directional version was a real trap.** It first read `<`, which catches only the INSERT case. After a DELETE the wall has *fewer* panels than the tiler would give, so the guard read false, the tiler path ran, and **the tiler put the deleted panel back** — silently, summing correctly. Bringing a count *down* is this stage's headline capability and typing widths is Stage 1's whole point, so on a 60-panel job those two gestures interleave on the same wall and would have cancelled with no notice at all.

**A rider the plan did not mention: slot-index coverage.** A Mid-Wall Bond Beam's coverage (either story) and the roofline Box Beam's are slot-index ranges, and an insert/delete shifts every index after it. `shiftSlotCoverage` moves them so they cover the same panels; a panel placed exactly at either edge lands outside the range; a delete that empties a range removes it and **says so in the notice**. Deliberately NOT extended to re-tiles, where the run is re-derived wholesale and coverage is a rough position at best.

**⚠ And it has to apply EVERY move, not the net one — also a review fix.** The first version shifted only when the array's length moved by exactly the delta the user asked for, so an insert the automatic run could only pay for by giving up panels (a 96in Big Header onto four 30in panels takes a wall from 6 slots to 4) got **no shift at all**, leaving a beam over panels it never covered or past the end of the array. `redistributeFreeRun` now returns `droppedIndices`/`droppedTypes` — which a caller cannot reconstruct — and the caller composes the real move list: the user's own +1/-1, then one -1 per dropped panel, highest index first.

**What an insert on a full wall does, stated because it will look like a bug.** A wall with no slack cannot hold another panel: the automatic run gives one (or more) up to pay for the new one and the wall's panel count does not move, or even falls. **The notice says so, and says what was given up** ("The automatic run gave up 2 panels (1 of them braced) to pay for it, so this wall now has 15 panels — narrow a panel to make room for another"), because the alternative is Tommy counting panels on a drawing to find out. The route to a higher count is the one the plan describes: pin widths narrower than the Standard width (Stage 1) and the freed budget shows up as room.

**Three known limits, none of them hidden:**

- **Only the paths this stage touches preserve the count.** The click-through cycle (`handleToggleOpening`), a window/Big Header width edit and a wall-length edit still re-tile and can take a hand-placed panel — or a hand *deletion* — with them. The new tool covers type changes on its own, so the workflow does not require the cycle; but this is the obvious next rider, and the real fix is still the plan's own "generalize `OpeningAnchor` to a slot anchor". **What IS covered, in both directions, is the typed width edit and the per-panel reset** (`retileWallAroundPins`).
- **The free run re-tiles FLAT.** Every automatic panel ends up within an eighth of every other, which means the "one absorber next to the gap, full width everywhere else" shape of a tiler-laid wall does not survive a hand edit. Nothing moves out of [24in, 48in], and the absorber's *position* rule (never corner-adjacent) is unaffected since positions do not move. **A hand-edited wall genuinely is different from a fresh one, so looking different is honest** — but nobody should later report it as a tiler regression; see Open Items.
- **A replace is re-tiled where it can be and refused where it cannot.** Turning a 72in window into a Standard panel gives its width back to the run it joins (four slots, 192in, 48/48/48/48); doing the same on a wall whose only free slot would be that panel is refused, because 72in is not a panel the shop can build and splitting it into two is not what one click asked for. **⚠ The refusal is the safe half and it was already right; the RE-TILE half is a review fix.** `redistributeFreeRun`'s "nothing has to move" shortcut fired on exactly this case — converting a fixed slot into a free one at the same width makes "same count" and "same budget" true by construction — so a **72in "standard" panel committed with no refusal and no notice**, contradicting this module's own header and `resolvePanelInsert`, which refuses that width outright. Nothing downstream would have caught it: `findSubMinimumPanelWidths` reports the FLOOR only and the app has **no over-maximum reporter at all**, so it would have reached a cut list. The shortcut now also requires every free slot to already be inside [24in, 48in].

**Verified:** `npx tsc --noEmit` clean in `apps/web`, `npx vitest run` green (114 files, 2101 tests, up from 2040), and a new in-repo browser harness — `apps/web/harness/smearforn-stage-2/` — 9 of 9 against the real app, including the wall total conserved to the eighth across insert/replace/delete, the safety-gap refusal in the words the tool prints, an 8ft Big Header refused with the real free width in the message, the panel-boundary drag standing down for Delete as well as for a placement type, and no uncaught exception in the page all run. It found two real defects on the way: ten tool buttons overflowing a 240px sidebar, and a corner step clicking the leftmost panel on a wall that owns no corner. **Stage 0/1's own harness was re-run against this branch as a regression check — 12 of 12, including all eleven ADU widths and the per-panel reset.** Its checked-in `evidence.json` and screenshots **were replaced**, and deliberately: that harness was itself fixed on this branch (see below), and the old artefact had been produced by a reader now *proven* to under-report, so keeping it would have preserved a `wallsWalked` figure from a broken reader and called it evidence. The replacement run carries `cpuThrottle: 8`, so the artefact demonstrates the fix under the condition that exposed the bug rather than leaving that proof in prose. (An earlier draft of this paragraph said the evidence had been left alone. It had been, at the time; commit `4fa5e87` made it false, and a claim outliving the thing it described is the same defect this stage's review kept finding.)

**A refusal on this path quotes the number.** The width edit's own fallback used to say "that couldn't be applied" and stop — and it is not a rare path: delete a panel from a 16-28ft wall and the automatic panels sit at 46¾-47⅜in, where **the narrowest pin the wall will take is 44½in**, so every width on the Rogers-Sehorn schedule (43in and down) is refused. `narrowestAcceptablePinWidthIn` (in `panelPlacement.ts`) answers that exactly, by asking `redistributeFreeRun` one eighth at a time rather than deriving a formula that would stop being right the first time the free-run rule changes; the refusal itself is now the same numbered sentence the placement tool prints, shared by both so they cannot drift. It reports what the arithmetic says and **never suggests a width** — a null answer means there is no width, not "try something else".

**Reviewed before merge, and the review found four things worth having** — two of them Monday-blocking, both already described above: the one-directional rider that let a delete be undone, and the shortcut that committed a 72in "standard" panel. The other two: the fallback path was returning before `retileWallAroundPins`' own wall-length check (so that guard was true of one path and not the other, against its own doc comment — it matters the moment Stage 3 changes what a wall's tiling length IS), and the drag strips were still drawn with **Delete** armed, so a click near a panel edge started a resize instead of deleting. The drag strips are now drawn only when no tool is armed at all, done by guarding the loop rather than widening the early return — in fact the early return is gone, so a later pass appending to that function (Stage 3's unbuilt-span line) cannot have its elements silently skipped while a tool happens to be armed.

**Flags check, run against the built diff: clean.** `data.ts` is not touched and no `CatalogValue`/`CatalogRange`/`PanelStructuralStatus` is in scope — the two catalog numbers this stage depends on (`fabricationMinPanelWidthIn` 24in, `panelWidthInRange.maxIn` 48in) are read, never redefined, and the pure module takes them as parameters. The widths a placed panel is born at are all existing values with their existing statuses: the project's Standard width, `COLUMN_TOTAL_WIDTH_IN`, and `bigHeaderDefaultWidthIn`/`bigHeaderDefaultHeightIn` (still `pending-BI-confirmation`, unchanged, and the tool does not present them as anything else). No fastener spacing, load, density, dimension or cost figure moves; nothing new reaches the Review Log. Every number added by the diff is a render or layout figure (a marker colour, a 2px stroke, an 8-second notice timeout) or index arithmetic.

**ADU reach after Stage 2, honestly:** panel *types* are now directly selectable anywhere on a wall, a wall's count can come **down** to match the schedule, and it can go **up** wherever the pinned widths have left slack. The triple headers are still Stage 2b.

---

Tommy: *"There should be a way to add a panel, select which type of panel you want to add, and then click where to put it. This would either replace a panel or add one between."*

- **Tool shape:** pick a type from the left bar, then click a panel or a boundary. Clicking a **panel** replaces it; clicking a **boundary** inserts between. Both are the anchor mechanism; neither is a new model.
- **Replace already half-exists.** `nextPanelCycleState` (`tiling.ts:603`) cycles standard → window → door → column → big-header → 4 braced styles → standard, and `handleToggleOpening` already routes width-changing transitions through the anchor retile and non-width-changing ones through an in-place mutation. The new tool is a **direct-select version of that same cycle** — no new transitions, no new types.
- **Placeable types: standard, braced (4 styles), window, door, column, big-header.** The click-cycle roster exactly.
- **NOT placeable: corner and safety-gap.** Both are placed by rules that exist for reasons — corner ownership (shorter-wall-wins, reflex corners, the merged-corner case) and gap-end placement. Hand-placing one would put the user in a fight with two systems that will overwrite them. **⚠ The ADU annotates "SAFETY GAP" repeatedly, so this may be exactly what Tommy wants next** — see Open Items. The anchor mechanism would carry it; it is a scope call, not a technical one.
- **Insert: where the width comes from.** A new panel is born pinned, at the project's standard width (or the type's own default — a Big Header is 96in by `bigHeaderDefaultWidthIn`). That width is reserved out of the budget and the free run re-tiles smaller. **If the free budget cannot cover it, refuse the insert** and say how much room there is. Never overflow the wall; never shrink a corner or an opening to make room.
- **Delete** is the same operation inverted: the slot goes, its width returns to the free run, the wall re-tiles. Deleting an opening is already expressible (cycle it back to standard); deleting a *panel* is new and is what lets a wall's count come down to match a drawing.
- **Neighbours:** untouched in type, style, zones and pins. Only the unpinned free run resizes. That is the whole point of the anchor design and it is the acceptance criterion.

**ADU reach after Stage 2:** panel *counts* become exact, so all four wall runs can be made to match the schedule. **The triple headers are NOT reachable here** — they are a cross-column relationship, not an insert; see Stage 2b.

### The triple header — SETTLED 2026-09-24, and it is a relationship, not three adjacent panels

Tommy: a triple header is **one header panel spanning two panels below it.** Verified in the cut list, and the arithmetic closes exactly:

| Panel | What it is |
|---|---|
| **E4A** | the header — two 6'5½" headers plus a lid |
| **E4B** | 3'5½" wide, below |
| **E4C** | 3'0" wide, below |

**3'5½" + 3'0" = 6'5½"** — the header's span is exactly the two panels beneath it. So A is not a sibling of B and C; **A sits on top of B and C.** An earlier draft of this section guessed "three adjacent Big Header slots" and would have produced a wall 6'5½" too long. Recorded because the guess was plausible and wrong, which is the dangerous combination.

**What the app can and cannot express today.** A `PanelSlot` is a full-height column, and `PanelSlot.zones` splits a column *vertically* — so "a header above a panel" is already expressible **within one column**, and "a header above two columns" is not. What spans a slot *range* today is a **Mid-Wall Bond Beam**: a `MidWallBeam` carries a slot-index coverage range (the `BoxBeamCoverage` shape), and `computeWallVerticalBandsForSlot` already shortens every covered slot's panels to make room for it. That is structurally the same object as a triple header.

**The design — CONFIRMED by Tommy 2026-09-24: *"Yes, that's what it is."*** Put to him as a header covering a slot range and reusing the mid-wall-beam coverage mechanism. A triple header is a **wall-level record over a slot-index range**, exactly like a mid-wall beam, except the thing occupying the band is a real **Header panel instance with its own width (the span), its own weight and its own fabrication sheet** — not a beam. **It began as an inference off the cut list's arithmetic and is now first-hand.** It appeared as an open question three times and should stop being re-listed: **Stage 2b is unblocked on geometry as well as on naming.**

Three consequences worth stating before anyone builds it:

- **It makes the A/B/C naming fall out naturally** — the spanning panel and the panels beneath it are a parent and its children, which is precisely the relationship a suffix expresses. See the nomenclature workstream: this is the same question, and Tommy has opened it.
- **`bigHeaderWidthInRange` (48–144in) is already `pending-BI-confirmation`**, noted "Tommy's own stated range — not mfr-sourced". A 6'5½" span sits inside it. **If a later job spans past 12ft, the range does not get widened to fit a drawing.**
- **`W4A` is an A with no B**, which under this reading means a header spanning something that was never split — or a naming artifact. Per Tommy, the ADU's letters came from splitting panels while leaving neighbours' names alone, so an orphan A is exactly the kind of debris that scheme produces. **Evidence for the nomenclature workstream, not a modelling requirement.**

**The label format question moved to the nomenclature workstream and was settled there: `E4`, hyphen dropped.** The spanning header itself is named from a **separate building-wide series (`H1`, `H2`) carrying no direction at all** — so **Stage 2b does not name it after E4, or after E, or after the east wall in any way**. That is the detail most likely to be assumed otherwise, and it is why the header's sheet has to state its wall in words.
