## Top Bar & App Chrome — the Stitch reorganisation (2026-09-13) — Stage 1 BUILT (overflow fix); Stage 2 BUILT (wordmark + nav at 1200px, name grows — see Tommy's 2026-09-13 decisions); Stage 3 BUILT (footer — role disclaimer, no policy links yet; sidebar/tray re-skin not done)

Two things arrived at the same answer: a real overflow bug that hides the sign-in control, and the Stitch mockups (`part 1 ui stitch/` and `part 2 ui stitch/`, each holding `code.html`, `screen.png` and a **byte-identical** `DESIGN.md`). **Stitch's header is not a restyle of today's bar — it is structurally smaller, and that is what fixes the bug.** Recorded as one decision so the fix is not improvised twice.

### The bug, measured

`TopBar.module.css`'s `.row` is a single `flex-wrap: nowrap` row with `overflow-x: auto`. Measured on the live site: **the row needs 1407px**. In a **710px** viewport it overflows by **697px**, and because `AccountControl` is the **last child in the row**, it is the first thing to fall off — **677px past the right edge**. Tommy could not find how to sign in; that is why.

**This is not merely inconvenient, it breaks a decision already made.** The backend section requires the acting-as company to be *"visible at all times, not buried in a menu,"* because the failure it prevents — saving a project into the wrong company's folder tree — is silent, plausible, and noticed later by someone else. **A control you must scroll sideways to find does not satisfy that.** `AccountControl.tsx`'s own doc comment already claims "always visible"; today the CSS makes that claim false.

Two smaller things fall out with it:

- **`overflow-x: auto` is itself a trap and goes away.** Per the CSS spec, setting one axis to a non-`visible` value forces the other to `auto`; that already caused one shipped bug (nested popovers clipped into the bar's 56px height — see `TopBar.tsx`'s doc comment and the `StickyNote` pattern that replaced them). Once the bar fits by construction the scroller has no job left, and removing it converts a future overflow from **silent off-screen content** into **visible breakage**. Same principle this log applies to silent rounding and to cost redaction: a visible gap beats a plausible-looking nothing.
- **There is no responsive story today.** The one rule, `@media (max-width: 900px) { .row { justify-content: flex-start } }`, changes the alignment of a row that already does not fit. Nothing collapses at any width.

### Evidence the design was drawn against this app, not at it

Worth stating because it changes how much of Stitch to take literally. **Three of its spacing tokens are already the app's own numbers:** `topbar-height: 56px` = `--topbar-height: 56px` in `globals.css`; `sidebar-width: 240px` = `.editorSidebar`'s `flex: 0 0 240px`; `tray-width: 170px` = `SectionCarousel.module.css`'s `width: 170px` and `.editorRightSpacer`'s matching 170px. Backend Stage 1 also landed the **chrome token layer** in `globals.css` using DESIGN.md's own Material-style vocabulary (`surface`, `surface-container-lowest`…`highest`, `on-surface`, `outline`, `primary`, `secondary`) under a `--bi-` prefix, with today's rendered values as defaults so nothing moved visually. **This pass is what starts consuming that layer.**

**The hard rule from the theming decision is unchanged and governs everything below: chrome re-skins, drawing semantics never do.** Member colours by role, material colours, the floor opacity bands, `pending-amber`, the review-log red encode meaning. A stud must not change colour because of who is looking.

### The decision this pass turns on — where the account / acting-as control lives

The Stitch mockups predate auth and have no such control, so there is nothing to copy. **Decision: the header becomes three zones, and the account control lives in the LEFT zone, immediately after the wordmark.**

| Zone | Contents | Shrink behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| **Left — identity & document** | Wordmark (1200px and up) · **Acting as ▾ / Sign in** · **Project ▾** | the account control and Project never shed; the name truncates before anything disappears |
| **Middle — scope** | Wall · Foundation · Floor · Roof | sheds whole, below 1200px *(was `md`; see "Tommy's decisions, 2026-09-13")* |
| **Right — presentation** | **Role: ▾** · ⚙ settings · ? help | sheds only the help icon |

**Why left, stated as reasons rather than taste:**

1. **It is the only placement that cannot reproduce the bug.** In an LTR overflow the rightmost content falls off first. Today's control is last in the row; that is the entire cause. Putting it first makes it the last thing that could ever be lost.
2. **It keeps the two role axes at opposite ends, and now for a structural reason rather than by luck.** `TopBar.tsx` already sites them apart deliberately ("those are the two axes that must never be merged, and sitting them side by side is how someone starts reading one as a level of the other"). Under the zone model the separation stops being a seating chart and becomes a taxonomy: **permission lives in the identity zone, presentation lives in the presentation zone.** Stitch puts `Role:` on the right; if the account control went right too, they would be adjacent dropdowns — the exact conflation the spec forbids.
3. **The theme decision already points this way.** The theme follows the company you are **acting as**, so eventually the whole interface colour is an ambient acting-as indicator. Sitting the company name against the wordmark makes brand + company read as one identity block, which is what the colour shift will reinforce.
4. **It is the document-header convention, not the SaaS convention.** This app's own printed output puts the producing party at top-left (`SheetTitleBlock`'s wordmark). The on-screen header matching that is coherent.

**The cost, accepted:** account-at-top-right is the more common web convention, and the wordmark is no longer flush against an empty left margin. Judged smaller than any of the four reasons above.

**Rejected, with reasons — recorded so they are not re-proposed:**

- **Absorbed into the ⚙ settings icon.** Directly violates "visible at all times, not buried in a menu." Not a trade-off; a contradiction of a decision already taken. **Do not build this even as an interim.**
- **Right end, after `Role:` (the conventional spot).** Two failures: it sits the permission axis against the presentation axis as visually-matched dropdowns, and it re-creates the exact geometry that produced this bug — last-in-row, first-to-fall. Survivable with a non-shrinking right zone, but it is the placement with the worst failure mode for no gain beyond familiarity.
- **Its own fixed element outside the header** (a floating chip). No home in either mockup; adds a fourth fixed chrome layer competing with the canvas, the sidebar and the tray in a permanently-fullscreen editor; and it detaches identity from the one place users look for it.

**Visual distinctness is a requirement, not a preference.** The acting-as control keeps its bordered chip (`--bi-surface-container-low`, uppercase "ACTING AS" caption, company by name). The viewer-role control takes Stitch's filled pill on `surface-container-high` and reads **"Role: Engineer"** — never bare "Engineer", which next to a company name reads as a job title or a permission level. The open role menu carries one line of prose: *changes which disclaimer prints; it is not a permission.* They must not become two matched dropdowns.

### Where the rest of today's bar goes

The split that decides it: **the Project menu holds things that change the building or the file. Settings holds things that change only how you look at it.**

| Today | Goes to | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Save Project · Load Project | **Project ▾** (left) | It is the file. Stage 2's cloud save / open / version history joins the same menu rather than needing a new home. |
| Site Properties | **Project ▾** | Zip, seismic zone, foundation type, pier spacing are design inputs that change the building — not preferences. |
| Panelizer | **Project ▾** | Holds the "keyhole" checkboxes that gate which editor tabs exist, plus panel width/thickness/density/wall height. Burying the project's core parameters under a gear icon would be wrong. |
| Imperial / Metric | **⚙ Settings** | Display-only by explicit decision (*"the unit toggle is display-only and never changes stored geometry"*), so it is a viewer preference. See Open Items — Tommy may want it back on the bar surface. |
| Admin Options (Show All Detail Pages) | **⚙ Settings**, still gated on `role !== "public"` | Tied to the viewer role, which is presentation. |
| Public/Fabricator/Admin/Engineer (4 buttons) | **Role: ▾** (one control) | This is Stitch's structural answer to the overflow: four buttons become one. |

Each menu keeps opening as a real `StickyNote`, exactly as today — that pattern exists because the old nested popovers were clipped by `.row`'s overflow, and a `position: fixed` note escapes the overflow context. **No new popover mechanism.**

**The ⚙ and ? buttons are icon-only and therefore need real accessible names** (`aria-label`), and a `title`. **Use inline SVG, not Material Symbols** — Stitch's markup pulls a Google webfont, which adds a network dependency, a FOUT, and a licensing question for a two-icon need. **The help icon has no content to show today**; see Open Items. Do not ship an icon that opens nothing.

### The editor tabs, and what happens to `EditorTabDial`

**Decision: the Wall/Foundation/Floor/Roof nav moves into the header's middle zone at 1200px and up; `EditorTabDial` is kept and is the below-1200px form.** Not deleted. *(Originally `md` = 768px. Measured not to fit without taking width from the acting-as company name — see "Tommy's decisions, 2026-09-13" below.)*

- Both are controlled by the same `editorTab` state in `page.tsx` — one source of truth, two presentations, **never both visible at once and never neither.**
- The header nav must honour the **same `enabledTabs` keyhole** the dial does (Panelizer's checkboxes gate Wall/Floor/Roof; Foundation is always included by the caller). A ruled-out tab is **absent from the nav**, not shown-and-inert.
- Keeping the dial is what makes the below-1200px story possible at all — Stitch marks its own nav `hidden md:flex` and simply offers nothing in its place, and the nav was measured not to fit beside the acting-as name until ~1200px (see Tommy's decisions, 2026-09-13). **Tommy's own 710px viewport is below 1200px**, so his everyday case is the one the dial covers.
- `EditorToolbar.tsx` is the dial's only wrapper and is Region 2 of the sidebar's documented three-region layout. Hiding it at 1200px and up shifts Region 3 upward — acceptable, because that happens at a breakpoint rather than during use, so Region 1's "height never varies" property survives.
- **Reversible.** If Tommy wants the dial gone entirely, it is a deletion at one call site, and the reverse (dial always visible, nav never) is the same size. Logged in Open Items.

### The responsive story — an explicit shed order

The bar must fit, without horizontal scroll, at every width down to **360px**. What sheds, in order:

1. **The nav tabs and the wordmark**, together, below 1200px → `EditorTabDial` appears in the sidebar. *(Was: nav below `md`, wordmark third. Changed 2026-09-13 by Tommy's decision: at `md` neither fits without taking width from the company name.)*
2. **The "ACTING AS" caption word.** The company name stays. **It goes below `md` (`max-width: 767px`), together with the carets and the tighter padding — before the company name loses any width.** Stage 1 first shed at 600px, and between ~601 and 700px the name was cut to "The See…" while the caption still showed: the order above, inverted. Corrected in review, 2026-09-13.
3. *(Now folded into step 1 — the wordmark sheds with the nav at 1200px.)* Originally: **the wordmark text** → nothing (no logo asset exists in the app today; `SheetTitleBlock` renders a text wordmark too). The acting-as / sign-in control takes the leftmost position, with Project ▾ after it. *(Corrected 2026-09-13: this line and the zone table above both put Project first, contradicting the decision they sit under — account control immediately after the wordmark. Stage 1 was built account-first and review confirmed that as the right reading.)*
4. **The help icon.**
5. **Nothing else.** The acting-as company name, the Project menu, the `Role:` control and the ⚙ icon are **never shed at any width.** If it still does not fit, the company name truncates with an ellipsis plus a `title` — **truncated but present beats absent**, which is the entire lesson of this bug.

**Breakpoint hygiene:** the app already has 900px (TopBar) and 600px (`page.module.css`, `EditorTabDial`). Stitch implies `md` = 768px. The 900px rule is deleted with the row it modifies; **do not invent a fourth number**, and write the two that remain in one commented block at the top of `TopBar.module.css`. Reconciling 768 vs 600 app-wide is out of scope this pass. **As built in Stage 1, the top bar uses only 768** (as `max-width: 767px`); 600 stays where it already was, outside the bar. **As built in Stage 2, the top bar changes at 1200 and 768, plus the 360px floor** — 1200 added knowingly by Tommy's 2026-09-13 decision. It is written as one `min-width: 1200px` condition that shows the nav and wordmark and (in `EditorToolbar.module.css`) hides the dial, rather than a `max-width: 1199px` / `min-width: 1200px` pair: two opposite queries both fail at a fractional viewport width such as 1199.5px under browser zoom, one condition cannot, so exactly one tab control shows at every width.

### Departures from the mockups, deliberate

A coder copying `code.html` would reintroduce shipped bugs. Named so they do not:

- **`dark:` variants are NOT adopted.** `part 1 ui stitch/code.html` carries them throughout. `globals.css` documents killing the boilerplate `prefers-color-scheme: dark` query after Tommy reported invisible button labels on a phone: *"This app has no actual dark theme (every component hardcodes light colors)."* Reintroducing dark classes reproduces that bug exactly.
- **The side panels stay flex children; they do not become `position: fixed`.** Stitch's `aside`s are fixed with `main` offset by margins. `page.module.css` says the opposite deliberately: *"both side columns are real flex layout space now, not absolutely-positioned overlays, so the canvas never renders underneath them."* Same visual result, and the app's version already survived the problem the mockup's version invites.
- **The sidebar does not disappear below `md`.** Stitch marks it `hidden md:flex`; the app narrows it to 64px at ≤600px, deliberately, so the tools stay reachable. Keep the app's behaviour.
- **The tray is not new work.** Part 2's 170px right `aside` is `SectionCarousel`, already built and already 170px. Part 1 has no tray, which is a difference between mockups rather than a decision to make. **Scope: the tray is re-skinned at most, never rebuilt.**
- **The wordmark must not use `header-gold`.** Stitch paints it `text-header-gold` (`#c9a63f`) — which in that same DESIGN.md is a **panel semantic** colour, sitting among `standard-panel`, `corner-panel`, `braced-panel`. Using it for the brand couples the wordmark to the header-panel colour, so re-theming one would move the other. **Use `--bi-primary` (navy), or add a dedicated `--bi-wordmark`.**
- **Mockup copy is not content.** "Project Alpha", "V1.0.4-Stable", "PL / Project Lead", "Building Integrity © 2024" are lorem. None of it ships.
- **`--topbar-height` stays exactly 56px.** `.main`, `SectionCarousel`, and `StickyNote`'s default spawn point *and* fullscreen state all measure against it. A bar that renders 57px tall drifts all four.

### Tommy's decisions, 2026-09-13 — the nav moves to 1200px, and the company name grows

**Why the original "nav at `md`" changed: it was measured not to fit.** Headless Chrome against the built Stage 1 bar, four companies, "Role: Fabricator": at 768px the row is 728px wide and needed 694px — left zone 503px with the company name at its 220px cap, right zone 181px — leaving **34px spare**. Stage 2 adds the wordmark (132px at headline-md) and four tabs (~250px), roughly **380px**. At `md` that could only come out of the company name, which the Stage 1 fix exists to protect. Every alternative (a later breakpoint, reordering the shed order, letting the name truncate, JS fit-detection) contradicted a line of this section, so the implementer stopped and it went to Tommy.

1. **Wordmark and nav at 1200px and up; `EditorTabDial` below.** A third top-bar width, chosen knowingly: the bar changes at 1200 and 768, plus the 360px floor. Below 1200 the bar is exactly Stage 1's. One CSS condition flips nav and dial in opposite directions, so exactly one shows; both render one shared definition (`editorTabs.ts`) from `page.tsx`'s one `editorTab` state.
   - **Tab type role, chosen by measurement at exactly 1200px** with all four tabs enabled, four companies, "Role: Fabricator": label-sm (12px/600) — nav 246px, name 270px, full label; **body-lg (14px/400) — nav 254px, name 270px, full label — chosen**; headline-md (16px/600, Stitch's own header role) — nav 292px, name 242px, above 220 but cutting "(platform admin)" at the boundary. body-lg is the largest role that keeps the full label readable at 1200. The current tab is marked by navy text and a 2px underline, not by weight, so switching tabs never changes the bar's width.
2. **The acting-as company name grows at 1200px and up.** Tommy: use the spare room so the "(platform admin)" / "(consortium)" tag is readable — it is what tells acting-as-Seed apart from belonging to Seed. Below 1200 the 220px cap is unchanged. At 1200 and up the cap is **280px**: "The Seed Collaborative (platform admin)", the longest real label, renders at 270px (13px/600 Geist, including the select's arrow), plus 10px. The nav, Project, Role and ⚙ do not shrink; only the name can give, so growth can never push a control off-screen. A longer company name than today's truncates at 280px and needs re-measuring. Layout measurements, not building values.

### The footer legal bar — built 2026-09-13 without the policy links (originally deferred; reasons kept below)

Stitch adds a fixed footer on `warning-red` carrying "Engineered Scope View", a provenance line, and Privacy Policy / Legal Disclaimer links. The app has no footer today. **Not in this pass.** It is a good idea with three unresolved dependencies, none of which are layout:

1. **There are no Privacy Policy or Legal Disclaimer documents.** Those are real legal texts; they are not mine to draft and not the coder's to stub. Needs Tommy.
2. **It costs canvas height in a permanently-fullscreen editor, and four things measure against the top bar only.** A footer needs a matching `--footer-height` consumed by `.main`, `SectionCarousel`, `StickyNote`'s spawn point and its fullscreen state, or it overlaps them. That is the same drift class `--topbar-height` was introduced to end.
3. **The disclaimer strings do not fit.** `roleDisclaimers[role].text` runs to ~200 characters for `engineer`, and DESIGN.md's own rule is that legal text never drops below 11px. Stitch's footer is 24px tall. So either the footer carries a short badge with the full text staying where it is, or it is taller than the mockup. A real decision, not a CSS detail.

**Hard rule whenever it does land: the footer renders `roleDisclaimers[role].text` verbatim. Those strings are the app's legal posture and may be relocated but never reworded.** Editing one is a legal change wearing a layout change's clothes. Its red is **chrome** (a banner), so it may take `--bi-error`; it is not the review-log red, which encodes meaning and stays hardcoded.

**As built (Stage 3, 2026-09-13).** How each of the three blockers was handled:

1. **Policy links: not built.** No Privacy Policy or Legal Disclaimer page and no `#` links. `AppFooter.tsx` has a commented slot at the right end of the strip for them. Waiting on Tommy's documents (Open Items).
2. **Height: `--footer-height: 24px`** (`globals.css`), the Stitch footer's own height. It is used everywhere `--topbar-height` measures the top edge: `.main`'s `bottom` (`page.module.css`), `SectionCarousel`'s `bottom`, `StickyNote`'s `.noteFullscreen` `bottom`, and the **spawn state** through an inline `max-height: min(75vh, calc(100vh - spawnTop - var(--footer-height) - 12px))` in `StickyNote.tsx`. Before this, a note spawned low on a short viewport ran under the bottom edge. The cap follows the spawn position, not the drag position, so a note does not resize while being dragged.
3. **Disclaimer length: solved in layout, not text.** The footer renders `roleDisclaimers[role]` by reference (`footerDisclaimer.ts`, with a test that the object and strings are identical). The strip is one line at 11px (the floor), and the text is the only thing that shrinks, ending in an ellipsis. **The whole strip is a button:**
   - its accessible name and `title` are the full text
   - clicking, tapping, or Enter opens the full wrapped text in a panel that grows **upward** from the strip; the strip or Escape closes it.

   The strip never changes height, so `--footer-height` stays constant. The footer's z-index (600) sits above a fullscreen note (500); otherwise the upward panel would open underneath one.

**Colour.** New chrome tokens `--bi-footer-surface: var(--bi-error)` and `--bi-footer-label: var(--bi-on-error)`. `--bi-on-error: #ffffff` is also new, from DESIGN.md's `on-error`. Stitch's `warning-red` (#c0392b) is **not** used: DESIGN.md lists it next to `pending-amber` and the panel colours, which is the semantic family. `error-container` was only its `dark:` variant, and `dark:` is not adopted. `#a33` is untouched. The footer is wrapped in `print-hidden-chrome`, like the top bar.

**Verified in headless Chrome** at 1920, 1280, 1200, 1199, 768, 710, 600 and 360 (900px tall), four companies, every role:
- **Layout:** zero page overflow on both axes; top bar 56px; footer 24px and fully on-screen.
- **Nothing under the footer:** `.main`, the tray, six cascaded spawned notes, and a fullscreen note all end at or above its top edge. At 600 and 360 the spawn cap engaged, with notes stopping 12px above the footer.
- **Disclaimer text:** verbatim in the strip, its `title`, and the expanded panel. The panel is on-screen, needs no scrolling, and is not covered, including over a fullscreen note. It tracks role changes.
- **Top bar name width:** unchanged from Stage 2 (270px at ≥1200; 220px from 1199 to 600; 71.9px for Fabricator at 360).
- **Print:** the footer renders nothing under print emulation. A print-targeted note's layout is identical with and without both Stage 3 changes (footer node removed, inline max-height cleared).

The engineer text truncates at 768 and below; the other three roles truncate only at 600 and below.

### Staging — the bug fix ships alone

**Stage 1 — Overflow and the account control.** The three zones, the non-shrinking left and right, the shed order, four role buttons → one `Role:` control, Project and ⚙ menus, `overflow-x: auto` removed, `AccountControl` pinned in the left zone. **This is the whole bug fix and it is shippable on its own.** No wordmark, no nav, no restyle.
**Stage 2 — The Stitch header shape.** Wordmark, the Wall/Foundation/Floor/Roof nav in the middle zone, `EditorTabDial` demoted to below-1200px (was below-`md`; see Tommy's 2026-09-13 decisions), `TopBar.module.css`'s hardcoded hex migrated onto the existing `--bi-*` tokens, Geist type roles applied to the bar. **Built 2026-09-13**, per Tommy's decisions above: wordmark and nav at 1200px and up, `EditorTabDial` below, one shared `editorTabs.ts`; the company name's cap rises to 280px at 1200px and up; `TopBar.module.css` on the `--bi-*` tokens (no visual change); Geist roles (wordmark headline-md, controls body-md, tabs body-lg by measurement, menu titles label-sm); `AccountControl.tsx` uses `clampMenuLeft` and re-clamps its note on resize. No help icon (nothing to open). **Verified in headless Chrome** at 1920, 1440, 1280, 1200, 1199, 1024, 768, 767, 710, 640, 600 and 360, signed out and with four companies, all four roles, all four scope tabs enabled: zero page and row overflow, header 56px, account control inside the viewport, exactly one of nav/dial with tabs in sync from either, every menu on-screen, company name 220px from 1199 to 600 and identical to Stage 1 at 360, and the full "The Seed Collaborative (platform admin)" (270px) at every width from 1200 up. Still for Tommy on the live build: whether the dial should survive at desktop width (Open Items).
**Stage 3 — Footer, and the rest of the chrome.** Blocked on the three footer questions above; the sidebar and tray re-skin rides here. Nothing in Stage 3 is urgent. **Footer built 2026-09-13** (see "As built" under the footer legal bar above): role disclaimer verbatim, `--footer-height` consumed by all four bottom-edge consumers, no policy links. **Not done in that pass:** the Privacy Policy / Legal Disclaimer links (awaiting Tommy's documents), and the sidebar and tray re-skin, which was not part of the footer handoff.

**Explicitly not in scope for any of the three:** the sidebar's *contents*, the tray's *contents*, the canvas, `ViewerDial`, per-company theme *values* (only the token layer is consumed), and any change to `viewerRole.ts`'s strings.

**Flags check: expected clean, verified against the code rather than assumed.** No `CatalogValue`, `CatalogRange` or `PanelStructuralStatus` is in scope; `data.ts` is not touched; no fastener spacing, load, density, dimension or cost figure moves; nothing new reaches the Review Log. Every number in this section (56px, 240px, 170px, 768px, 600px, 360px) is a layout measurement, not a building value. The one thing to watch: `roleDisclaimers` text is legal-posture content — it may be **relocated or re-presented, never edited** — and the redaction-adjacent principle applies to the bar as much as to the server, in that a control which is present-but-off-screen is the UI equivalent of a plausible substituted number. The coder re-runs the 6-point check against the actual diff.

### "Speaking of which, where is it?" — the Panelizer, answered

**It is not a tab and never has been. It is a menu item inside `Project ▾`.** `TopBar.tsx:413-420` renders a `Panelizer` button inside the Project note, which opens a second `StickyNote` (`TopBar.tsx:428-430`) holding `panelizerContent` (`page.tsx:6304-6727`). That is why it is hard to find: it is **two levels deep behind a menu named after files**, and its own doc comment describes it as *"the keyhole to getting down to what editor tools are needed for this user's project"* — i.e. the most consequential control in the app, filed under Save/Load.

**So his instruction and the defect agree, and the move is the fix, not a preference.** Panelizer content goes to Settings, one level deep, with Site Properties and the Single Wall Run sandbox beside it.

### THE CENTRAL REQUIREMENT — "let's make sure nothing is lost"

**That is a checkable claim, and making it checkable is this plan's main job.** The inventory below was built by **reading the code**, not by reasoning about what an app like this probably has. Every row has a destination or is named as an Open Item. **This inventory is the acceptance criterion for the whole workstream** and it is what a reviewer checks against.

**A navigation change has one specific failure mode: something stops being reachable and nobody notices.** It does not throw, it does not render wrong, and it does not fail a unit test — the same fail-quiet class this log has already paid for twice (`orderedWallCycle` returning `null` and emitting no floor framing; the account control sitting 677px off-screen while its own doc comment claimed "always visible"). **The staging below is arranged so the right sidebar — today's home for every printable — is the last thing deleted**, which means there is a working fallback in front of the user during every intermediate stage.

##### 9a. The left bar's bottom cluster — DECIDED 2026-09-26

Tommy, 2026-09-26:

> *"Let's make a cute fat outline of a log icon with the word review on it (review log lol) and add that near the ? On the bottom left."*

> *"Report bug / feature request backend sounds like a great idea. Right now it goes to a note that is easy enough right now - referring people to email me. Let's consider backend improvements to that as a flagged thing to do later. For now, can we add a cute outline of a bug that opens up a sticky note with the current page contents on it?"*

**So the bottom-left cluster becomes four icons, in the same outline style as the existing `?`:**

| Icon | Opens | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `?` | `PageFeaturesButton` — the per-tab `pageFeatures` list | Already built. Unchanged, still bottom-pinned by `marginTop: auto` |
| **Review** — *"a cute fat outline of a log icon with the word review on it"* | The **Review Log** section | **This closes the gap this plan flagged.** Safety-relevant output now has its own front door in the chrome, not a slot inside Summary or Print |
| **Bug** — *"a cute outline of a bug"* | A **sticky note** carrying the existing report-bug content **plus the current page's name** | Backend deferred — see the flagged item below |
| **Read Me** — *"its own cute little icon"* | The **Read Me** content | §9b on why a note rather than a navigation |

**Why the Review Log icon is the right answer and not just a convenient one.** The Review Log is `toReviewLog()`'s output — *"Items for Engineer/Contractor Review"* — which is where every `pending-BI-confirmation` value and every sub-minimum panel width surfaces. **Flags-check point 5 requires that gaps surface where a human reviewer expects them.** A section reachable only by scrolling a 170px strip that is about to be deleted was already the weak link; giving it a permanent icon strengthens point 5 rather than merely relocating it.

**The bug note — two hard constraints.**

1. **The existing wording is preserved verbatim.** `/report-bug/page.tsx` already exists as a real route: a heading, an attribution line, two sections (*"Found a bug or glitch?"* / *"Have an idea for a feature?"*) each with a numbered ask and a `FOR EXAMPLE:` block, a closing *"Please include the date noticed/idea conceived and send to:"* line with a `mailto:` address that **is already in the file**, and two links (back to the editor, and `/?openNote=review-log`). **Reuse that content by reference; do not rewrite, tighten or "improve" it, and introduce no address that is not already there.** The `Review Log` link inside it should now point at the same surface the new Review icon opens.
2. **The page context must be honest, and it is not telemetry.** *"a sticky note with the current page contents on it"* is read as: **the note names the view the user was on when they opened it**, so the email he receives has context. Name it **as the app itself labels it** — the active `ViewerStop` label (`Plan View` / `Elevation: AB` / `3D Framed` / `3D Boxes` / `Membranes`), the active editor tab from `EDITOR_TAB_LABEL`, and — once they exist — `Summary`/`Print` when one of those owns the surface. **No version string, no user agent, no viewport dump, no diagnostic payload, no auto-send.** He asked for a note, not a reporter. *(If he meant only "the note as it currently reads", dropping the context line is a one-line change.)*

**FLAGGED FOR LATER — a report-bug/feature-request backend.** His words: *"Let's consider backend improvements to that as a flagged thing to do later."* Recorded here in the same style as the buck window and the SketchUp/DC export: **a decided deferral, not an open question.** What a later decision would need to answer, so that it is informed when it happens: **where a report goes** (a table, an email relay, or an issue tracker); **whether it needs its own table with RLS** — and if so, that every existing RLS pattern here is company-scoped while a bug report is not obviously a company's property; **whether the reporter's identity is attached**, which is a privacy question and not a schema one, and which interacts with the fact that reports can arrive from signed-out guests; and **whether anything from the project state travels with the report**, which would make a bug report a data export and put it straight into the redaction model's territory. **None of that is designed here and nothing in this workstream touches `supabase/`.**

##### 9b. Read Me and the bug note: notes, not navigations — and the reason is a real hazard

**Both `/read-me` and `/report-bug` are Next routes today**, linked from the tray footer. **There is no `localStorage` or `sessionStorage` anywhere in `apps/web/app` — verified by search, zero matches.** So **navigating to either route and coming back loses the entire in-memory design** unless it was saved to a file or the cloud first.

**That hazard exists today.** But this pass (a) deletes the tray those links live in, and (b) promotes them to always-visible icons in the editor chrome — i.e. makes them *more* likely to be clicked mid-drawing. **Recommendation: render both as sticky notes inside the editor, reusing the routes' content, and keep the routes in place** for direct linking and for printing. That is also exactly what Tommy asked for on the bug icon, so it is consistent rather than inventive.

**⚠ Two things in the Read Me content to handle, not flatten:** it carries a **liability statement** (*"anything coming from this app that you want to produce is your liability"*) — legal-posture text in the same family as `roleDisclaimers`, so **verbatim, never reworded** — and a **Venmo QR `Image` plus an "Open as PDF" link**. A QR code that renders too small to scan is a broken feature, so if Read Me becomes a note the QR needs the note's fullscreen path or its existing PDF link, whichever is verified to scan. *(Read Me as a note rather than a navigation is a recommendation, not something he said — Open Item.)*

#### 11. The label pattern — the precise rule

**What "look like the Acting As button" means, read off the CSS rather than guessed.** `AccountControl.module.css`: `.actingAsLabel` is **11px / 600 weight / `text-transform: uppercase` / `letter-spacing: 0.01em` / `--bi-on-surface-muted`** (his "all caps dark grey"), and the value is **13px / 600 / `--bi-on-surface`** (his "black"). **Reuse those two type treatments.** Do **not** reuse the rest of the control: the acting-as value is a `<select>` inside a bordered chip, whereas Design/View/Summary/Print are buttons that open `StickyNote` menus. **Take the typography, not the chip and not the select.**

**The owner rule — stated precisely, because his example implies it without stating it:**

- **Exactly one of Design / View / Summary / Print owns the editor surface at any moment.** Ownership is derived, never stored twice: `Design` owns when the surface is the drawing and `currentViewerStop.kind` is `plan` or `elevation`; `View` owns when it is `3d-framed`, `3d-boxes` or `3d-wraps`; `Summary` and `Print` own when their full page fills the editor.
- **The owner renders two parts:** `LABEL` in the caption treatment, then the current value in the value treatment, Title Case. **The other three render the bare word** in the ordinary control treatment.
- **So his two examples come out exactly as he wrote them:** `DESIGN Plan View · View · Summary · Print`, and after choosing 3D Framed, `Design · VIEW 3D Framed · Summary · Print`.
- **Summary's value is the summary section being read** — `SUMMARY Material Totals`. Summary opens on `Project Summary`, so there is always a real section label and **no default word has to be invented.**
- **Print shows no value, even when active.** He never gives Print one, and Print is one editor rather than a set of pages you are "on". It is marked active the way the nav tabs already are: **navy text plus a 2px underline, never by weight**, so switching never changes the bar's width. *(Stated as the reading; low-risk, worth one word from Tommy.)*

**⚠ The menu-contents sentence has two readings and only one is usable.** *"Each of these three drop down buttons along with print will only show the current page under it's button menu."* Read literally, a menu would list exactly one item — the page you are already on — which makes it impossible to change page. **Rejected on that ground.** The usable reading, and the one his own example supports (*"View and Summary just show view and Summary"* is about the **bar text**): **each menu lists its own stops and only its own stops, with the current one marked; the two-part LABEL+Value treatment appears on the bar only for the menu that owns the active page.** That is what "only show the current page under its button" is describing — the bar, not the menu body.

#### 12. ⚠ The width budget is already spent — the riskiest assumption in this plan

**His bar is twelve controls. The current bar needed a third breakpoint to fit six.** From this log's own measurements:

- At **768px**, Stage 1's bar (no wordmark, no nav) needed 694px in a 728px row — **34px spare**.
- The wordmark (132px) plus four tabs (~250px) is roughly **380px** more, which is **why the nav sits at 1200px and not at `md`** — Tommy's own 2026-09-13 decision, made because the only place that width could have come from was the acting-as company name, which the Stage 1 fix exists to protect.
- At exactly 1200px with all four tabs and four companies, the nav measured **254px** and the company name **270px**, with the bar fitting and little to spare.

**Design + View + Summary + Print add four more controls, one of which carries a two-part label up to the width of `Elevation: AB` or `3D Framed`.** On those recorded figures that is plausibly another **350–400px**, i.e. a bar wanting **~1550–1600px**. **No number here is measured — that is the point.** **And Tommy's own everyday viewport is 710px**, where today the nav and wordmark are already shed and `EditorTabDial` is doing the job.

**So: the twelve-item bar cannot exist at his own width, and it is not yet known to exist at 1200px.** Two consequences, both structural:

1. **Measurement comes first, in the same headless-Chrome way the 1200px breakpoint was established** — at 360, 710, 768, 1200, 1440 and 1600, signed out and with four companies, every role, every scope combination. **The measurement is a deliverable of the first stage, not a follow-up.**
2. **The shed order must be extended, and the existing one is not negotiable:** the acting-as company name, the file menu, the role control and Settings are **never shed at any width**, and *"truncated but present beats absent"* is the entire lesson of the 2026-09-13 bug. **Recommendation: Design/View/Summary/Print shed together into the left sidebar below the breakpoint, exactly as the tab nav already sheds into `EditorTabDial` — and the sidebar's existing `ViewerDial` is already the Design+View form of it.** One shared definition, two presentations, one CSS condition (not an opposed pair — a fractional viewport width under browser zoom fails both), never both and never neither. That also **keeps the scroll-wheel and the rustle sound alive at Tommy's own width**, which is the §7 row that would otherwise vanish.

**⚠ Do not invent a fourth breakpoint casually.** The bar has 1200 and 768 plus a 360px floor, written in one commented block in `TopBar.module.css`, and this log has an explicit "do not invent a fourth number" rule. If the measurement says the new group needs its own width, **that is a decision for Tommy with the measurement in hand**, the same way 1200px was.

#### 13. Summary and Print as full pages, with the edit tabs still live (his answer 4)

His answer: **Summary and Print fill the editor, and Walls/Floor/Roof/Foundation stay visible and clickable — clicking any of them returns you to the drawing. Not a modal mode.**

**What that requires of state, established by reading where the state lives:**

- **Add one piece of state — the editor surface: `"drawing" | "summary" | "print"`.** Nothing else moves. `editorTab`, `elevationViewWallId`, `viewMode`, `simplified3D`, `showWraps`, `viewedStoryId` and `selectedSlot` all stay in `page.tsx` and are not touched by opening Summary or Print, so returning restores the exact view — **including the current wall and the current story.**
- **⚠ But the drawing must be HIDDEN, not unmounted, and here is the concrete reason.** `FootprintCanvas` holds `viewOffset` and `viewScale` (pan and zoom), `showPanelLabels`, and the whole measuring-tool state **in its own component state**. `Building3DView` holds its camera the same way. **Unmounting the editor to show Summary silently resets the user's pan, zoom, label toggle and 3D camera** — a "nothing is lost" failure that no unit test would catch and that looks like a glitch rather than a bug. Lifting that state into `page.tsx` is the alternative and is much larger. **Hide it.**
- **Clicking an edit tab sets the surface back to `"drawing"` and sets `editorTab` in one action.** That is his "clicking any of them returns to the drawing", and it needs no new mechanism.
- **The four tabs stay visible while Summary/Print own the surface** — so the bar's tab group is not conditional on the surface.

**⚠ This collides with the keyhole, and the collision is real.** `editorTabsInScope(enabledTabs)` makes a ruled-out tab **absent** from the nav, by explicit decision (*"A ruled-out tab is absent from the nav"*), and **Smearforn Stage 0 turned Floor and Foundation OFF by default** — *"I would like the turn off the floor and foundation tools as default for now… This setting should still be visible, but perhaps it's somewhere in settings."* **So on a brand-new project today, two of the four tabs he lists do not exist on the bar.** Three possible readings, and this plan takes none of them on its own authority:

- (a) **Keep the keyhole.** The bar shows only in-scope tabs; his list describes the all-checked case. Smallest, changes nothing, and stays consistent with an existing decision.
- (b) **Always show all four**, and clicking an out-of-scope tab turns that scope branch on. Matches his list literally, but makes the tab bar a second writer of the Panelizer's scope state.
- (c) Always show all four, out-of-scope ones inert — **rejected here**, because "shown and inert" is the exact thing the existing decision rejected.

**Recommendation: (a), because it preserves a decision already taken and his answer 4 was about Summary/Print not stealing the tabs, not about the keyhole.** → **Open Item.** *(And note the Panelizer's scope checkboxes are what would drive (b), which is another reason the Panelizer belongs somewhere findable — §0.)*

#### 14. Print — what exists, and what a "fleshed out printing customization editor" is

**What exists today, in full:** the three tray-header controls (`Export PDF (n)`, `Choose sections ▾` over `exportableSections`, `Page size` Letter/Tabloid), the per-note `🖶` button on 27 sections via `handlePrintNote`, `openDetailPageIds` / `manualExportIds` / `effectiveExportIds` (default = "whatever is currently open", until the user touches the picker, after which it is an explicit set), the open-print-restore dance in `handleExportSelectedPdf`, the last-target marking that makes the packet's "no page break after the final section" rule work, `SheetTitleBlock` on the formal sheets, and `showAllDetailPages` (admin/fabricator) which widens the sheet list.

**Print's content is therefore already specified: it is `exportableSections` plus those three controls plus the per-sheet print button.** That part is a relocation and is fully spec'd by the inventory above.

**"Customization" is the least specified part of his whole request, and this plan says so rather than designing it.** What it plausibly covers, offered as a menu of candidates for him to choose from and **not** as a design: **which sheets** (already exists — `Choose sections`); **what order** (does not exist; sheets print in `relevantDetailPages` order, which is derived from what the design contains); **per-sheet options** (page size is global today, not per sheet); **a cover sheet / packet title**; **and the numbered continuation sheets that are already decided-but-not-built** — *"each continuation page is a real framed sheet with its own title block, numbered 'Sheet 2 of 3'"* — which is where the known page-overflow problem lives (Shipping, Plaster Master and Project Summary each run 1–2.5 pages over on any page size).

**⚠ Recommendation: Print ships as a full page holding exactly today's controls (stage U5), and the customization editor is its own later stage with its own plan (U6).** Two reasons: he described it in one clause, and the honest print blocker is pagination, not the picker — *"pagination is still unconfirmed: page breaks, fragmentation, and the packet blank-page fix are only observable in a real print preview."* **A customization editor built on top of unverified pagination would let a user arrange sheets that do not paginate.**

**U0 → U1 is the spine, and U5 is the point of no return.** U2, U3 and U4 are each independently orderable between them. **U0 can ship on its own at any time, including before admin tooling finishes** — it touches no shared surface, and the Review Log's front door has value the moment it exists. **U2 cannot start without Tommy's answer.**

### How big is this, honestly

**Roughly all of Smearforn Stages 0–3 — on the order of a week of agent work — with U6 excluded.** Against the ring workstream's ~3× Smearforn, this is about a third of that. Breaking it down: **U0 is the smallest real slice in the plan** (a day or so); **U1 is deceptively mid-sized** because the measurement and the shed order are most of it, not the menus; **U2 and U3 are relocations** and are genuinely small *if* U2's decision has already been made; **U4 and U5 together are the bulk**, more than half the total.

**Is any of it riskier than it looks? Yes, four things, and they are the reason for the staging:**

1. **The failure mode is unreachability, and unreachability is silent.** No error, no wrong number, no failing test. This app has already paid for this class twice (`orderedWallCycle` drawing no floor framing; the account control 677px off-screen while its own comment claimed otherwise). **The inventory plus a reachability harness is the mitigation, and neither is optional.**
2. **The width budget is already spent (§12).** The bar needed a third breakpoint to fit six controls; his list is twelve. **This is the single most likely thing to stop the plan mid-flight**, which is exactly why U1 measures it before anything depends on it.
3. **The three existing Smearforn harnesses will break.** They locate the view dial and the editor chrome by the strings and DOM this pass rewrites — and this log's own Open Items record the lesson: *"a reader keyed to an incidental element fails on legitimate data, and it fails by returning nothing rather than by raising anything."* **Fixing those locators is in scope for whichever stage breaks them, not a follow-up**, or the repo loses the harnesses that caught what unit tests could not.
4. **Every stage touches `page.tsx`, which is ~10,300 lines and on which ESLint OOMs at the default heap.** `apps/web/AGENTS.md` governs: typecheck **both** projects, run lint from `apps/web` with the raised heap, and **measure a lint delta including severity-1 warnings** against the base commit, because this file carries pre-existing errors (94 as of 2026-09-25) and a raw total means nothing.

### How it gets verified — a reachability harness

**A reorganisation's real risk is unreachability, which is exactly what a browser harness can walk.** The three in-repo harnesses (`apps/web/harness/smearforn-stage-0-1/`, `-stage-2/`, `-stage-3/`) are the standard: a CDP session against a real dev server, checked-in `evidence.json` and screenshots, `record()` **throwing** when given no expectation, a non-zero exit on any false expectation, **and both outcomes measured rather than assumed.** A `ui-reorg` harness should meet that bar and assert:

- **Reachability is exhaustive and counted, not sampled.** From a cold load, every id in `allNoteSections` and every `exportableSections` entry is reachable, and **the number of reachable sheet ids equals `relevantDetailPages.length + 3`** — a count, so a silently dropped section fails the run instead of going unnoticed. Repeat **per role** (`public` / `fabricator` / `admin` / `engineer`), since role changes the sheet list, and with `Show All Detail Pages` both off and on.
- **Every inventory row has a click path.** Site Properties, every Panelizer control group, Single Wall Run, the Review Log, Read Me, the bug note, Project Totals, and each of Tommy's six Summary sections — reached, and screenshotted.
- **The bar fits, at every width.** Zero page and row overflow at **360, 710, 768, 1200, 1440, 1600**, signed out and with four companies, all four roles, all four scope branches; top bar exactly 56px; footer exactly 24px; the acting-as company **inside the viewport at every width** — the assertion the 2026-09-13 bug exists to make permanent.
- **Exactly one presentation of each control at every width.** One of {bar tab group, `EditorTabDial`}; one of {bar Design/View menus, sidebar `ViewerDial`} — never both, never neither, checked at 1199 and 1200 and under a fractional zoom width.
- **The owner rule renders exactly as he wrote it.** `DESIGN Plan View · View · Summary · Print`, then `Design · VIEW 3D Framed · Summary · Print`, read out of the DOM.
- **Return-from-Summary preserves the drawing.** Pan and zoom (read the canvas transform), the selected wall, the story, and the 3D camera are identical before and after a Summary → tab-click round trip. **This is the assertion that catches the unmount-versus-hide mistake.**
- **`?openNote=review-log` still opens the Review Log**, since `/report-bug`'s own link depends on it.
- **The `🖶` path still prints one section**, and `Export PDF` still restores the prior open state afterwards.

### Flags check — run against this plan

Per the 6-point discipline. **This plan introduces zero new `CatalogValue`s and zero real-world building numbers, and that is not a coincidence — it is the test of whether the plan stayed in its lane.** If a presentation change ever finds itself needing a dimension, a density, a fastener spacing or a price, something has gone wrong.

1. **Every real-world number in the diff carries a `status` and a `note`** — **there are none.** Every number in this section is a layout measurement (56px, 24px, 240px, 170px, 64px, 220px, 280px, 360/710/768/1200/1440/1600px) or a count of sections. Same argument the Top Bar & App Chrome section already makes for its own figures.
2. **Anything marked `confirmed` that is actually interpreted?** Nothing is being marked. **⚠ The live risk here is different and specific: Site Properties and the Panelizer are the two densest displays of flagged catalog values in the app** — `seismicBracedPanelSpacingFt`, `bracedWallLineSpacingFt`, `groundScrewProductsStatus`, the `foundationTypes` vapor notes, `looseDensePackThicknessOptionsIn`, `targetDensityKgM3`, `fabricationMinPanelWidthIn`, `panelWidthInRange`, and the *"Default 10ft (120in) is Panel Set 1's confirmed standard panel height"* note. **Both move wholesale into Settings. They move BY REFERENCE. Not one value, one note, one `status` or one `pending` style is re-typed, re-rounded or re-worded in transit.** A relocation is the easiest possible moment to silently retype a number, which is why it is written down as a rule rather than assumed.
3. **Notes trace to a source?** Every figure quoted is read out of the code or out of this log's own measurement records, cited in place.
4. **Structural figures using `PanelStructuralStatus` with no invented value?** None is touched. `STRUCTURAL_PENDING_NOTE` stays where it is; the Selected Panel note's Material Specs block (straw density, framing size) moves nowhere.
5. **Do the gaps surface in the review log?** **This is the point this plan actively improves.** The Review Log is `toReviewLog()`'s pending-value output and today it is reachable only through a 170px strip that this pass deletes. **It now gets its own permanent icon in the chrome (§9a), plus a kept `?openNote=review-log` deep link, plus a harness assertion that it is reachable in every role.** Nothing new reaches the Review Log and nothing leaves it.
6. **Is the code treating open decisions as provisional?** Yes, and two in particular: **the acting-as visibility reversal (U2) does not get built until Tommy answers**, and **the keyhole question (§13) does not get resolved by whichever branch is easier to code.** Also: `roleDisclaimers` and the Read Me liability text are **relocated, never reworded** — *"editing one is a legal change wearing a layout change's clothes."*

**Not in scope, explicitly, for any stage:** anything in `supabase/`, `apps/web/app/auth/**`'s session logic or `apps/web/app/cloud/**`; `PROJECT_FILE_VERSION`; the Privacy Policy and Legal Disclaimer documents; any wording in `viewerRole.ts`; any catalog value; the canvas, the drawing semantics, the member colours, the panel colour legend or the floor opacity bands; the *contents* of any tool section in the left sidebar's Region 3; the report-bug backend; the numbered continuation sheets; and **the printing customization editor beyond U5's relocation of today's controls.**

- `isViewerDialLive`'s **name becomes wrong**, though the property it holds — one definition read by four call sites — is worth keeping under a better one. `viewerMenus.ts` and `viewLabels.ts` need re-reading against a dial-less app.

**5. The wordmark is expendable.** *"I don't think it's really all that important to have Building Integrity in left side. Maybe that would save a lot of space."* Worth ~142px **but only at ≥1200px, where it currently shows** — below 1200 it already sheds, so it buys nothing at his own 710px. It would pull a labelled Design/View threshold down by roughly its own width; against bare buttons its value is unmeasured.

**6. `useRustleSound()` may go with the dial.** *"The rustle sound is no big deal. I'll probably add sound effects to certain things at later dates, but not a big deal that we are moving on from that."* **Recorded as his decision so its absence is not later read as an oversight**, and so a future sound pass starts from "this was deliberately dropped" rather than "this was lost".

### ⚠ INTERVIEW OF 2026-09-28 — the menu structure, the engineer lens, and a real roof-panel spec

Tommy asked to interview and plan rather than keep building. These answers **supersede parts of the "Decisions of 2026-09-28" block above** where they conflict, and they open a new workstream.

#### The structure: ONE merged Design menu, GROUPED BY SUBJECT

**Decided.** The two axes collapse. Today the **tab** says what you are editing (Walls / Floor / Roof / Foundation) and the **view** says how you are looking at it (plan, elevation, 3D, membranes). They merge:

- **Design** holds every design destination, **grouped with headings by subject** — Walls (Plan View, then each wall elevation), then Floor, Roof, Foundation.
- **View** holds the generated representations — 3D Framed, 3D Boxes, Membranes.
- **No separate `Walls / Floor / Roof / Foundation` bar items.** This frees roughly **264px** of bar, the single biggest saving available, and it materially changes the width budget measured at U1.
- Grouping is what keeps a long list usable: with every scope on and an octagon drawn, Design would otherwise be a flat list of a dozen or more entries.

**Why grouped rather than flat:** he chose it over a flat list explicitly. The headings do the work the removed tabs used to do — they say *which subject* — while the menu still reaches everything from one control.

#### Scope gating: ALREADY BUILT, and defaulting the way he wants

His request was *"all floor, foundation, and roof options should be a checkbox toggle under settings… once you check them on, you can access it through the drop down menus"*, with floor/roof/foundation **hidden by default** because *"every job will include walls while some may include roof, floor, and foundations."*

**Verified in the code, 2026-09-28 — this is ~90% shipped:**
- `page.tsx` has `roofEnabled` (**default false**), `foundationEnabled` (**default false**), `floorsEnabled` and `wallsEnabled`, collected into a `scopeOfWork` object.
- `enabledEditorTabs` is derived from them, pushing foundation / floor / roof **only when enabled** — so unchecked scopes are already hidden from both the tab dial and the nav.
- The **Panelizer's own "keyhole" checkboxes** already drive it. His words, in the code: *"I want this tab to be the keyhole to getting down to what editor tools are needed for this user's project."*
- **U3 already moves the Panelizer into Settings**, which carries those checkboxes there with no extra work.

**So the genuine gaps are only:** the gating must now filter the **Design menu's groups** rather than a tab list, and `EditorTabDial`'s doc comment claiming *"Foundation has no such checkbox, so it's always included by the caller"* is **stale** — Smearforn Stage 0 added `foundationEnabled`.

#### The engineer lens: its own Summary section

**Decided.** The engineer lens gets **a dedicated engineering section in the Summary page** — every wall section and every panel with its equations and inputs: **stud pack, header bearing capacity, and shear**, wall-by-wall or per panel. One place to review a whole building's structure, separate from the shop-floor sheets.

His read on why the lenses feel clunky is worth keeping: *"i think my clunkiness feelings though are just to do with it having been visible before, which i believe were changing right now."* So the fix may be placement, not mechanism.

⚠ **This section must derive from the same computation the panel sheets already use.** The structural values on a fabrication sheet and the equations in Summary showing their working cannot come from two code paths, or they will disagree and the disagreement will be invisible. `PanelStructuralStatus` and the existing `pending-BI-confirmation` statuses ride along unchanged — **an equation shown beside a provisional value does not make it confirmed.**

#### Viewing-as: signed-out is public, signed-in defaults to architect, and the choice is REMEMBERED

**Decided.** A not-signed-in visitor can only view as **public**. Signing in defaults to **architect**. And he chose **remember what each person last selected** over resetting each session.

⚠ **"Remembered per person" has a cost he should see:** there is **no `localStorage` or `sessionStorage` anywhere in `apps/web`** (verified), and browser storage would be per-browser rather than per-person anyway. Per-person means the account record — `public.user_profiles` (`0001`), which today carries `email`, `display_name`, `is_platform_admin` and `created_at` and **has no preferences column**. So this needs **a migration and therefore a hand-paste from Tommy**, in the style of `0009`/`0010` with pre-flight and post-flight checks. Small, but it is the first migration since the platform-backup slice was found to need none. **Flagged, not assumed.**

##### The two levels of highlight, and why they are two functions

`viewerMenuOwner({ editorTab, currentStop })` — the BAR — and `isCurrentDestination(destination, { editorTab, currentStop })` — the OPEN MENU. Each has its own unit tests and its own browser acceptance criterion, and **neither is colour alone**: the bar carries `aria-pressed` plus an inset 2px underline (an underline, not weight, so ownership moving cannot reflow the row — the removed nav tabs' own recorded reason); the menu entry carries `aria-current="true"` plus heavier weight and a left edge bar. Asserted in the browser against a non-current sibling, not described in a comment.

⚠ **Ownership deliberately no longer reads the footprint, and that is a correction.** Tommy: *"When you open the app it'll automatically be in planview editor. This will make the design button highlighted."* Under U1's rule ownership required a live view stop, which requires a footprint — so **on a cold load neither menu was highlighted**, on the exact screen he was describing. The harness asserts the launch state first, before it draws anything.

##### One writer, with the dial gone

`handleViewerStopChange` is still the only writer of `viewMode` / `simplified3D` / `showWraps` / `elevationViewWallId`; `setEditorTab` is still the only writer of `editorTab`. The merged menu calls both and writes neither. **Half of U1's proof was impossible to keep** — it compared the dial against the menus inside one run — so:

- **Across the change**, unchanged and unrepeatable: `region3-baseline.json` was recorded off the **dial**, so comparing the menus against it is still a two-control comparison. It can never be re-made.
- **Two paths, one run**, the replacement: every stop is reached directly and again after a detour through a stop of the other kind, and Region 3 must be **byte-for-byte identical** both times, digits included. The detour is what writes the flags, so this tests precisely `showWraps` left true on a plan view arrived at from 3D.

##### The review's fixes — 2026-09-29, applied on the same branch

A review of the four U3 commits found one assertion recording a falsehood, one decision, and three smaller things. All five are fixed here; the order change is the only one that alters what a user sees.

**1. `ui-reorg-u0`'s reachability check was HORIZONTAL ONLY, under the name `onScreen`.** The predicate was `r.width > 0 && r.left >= 0 && r.right <= innerWidth` — no `top`, no `bottom` — and it reported `"onScreen": true, "passed": true` for a link the committed screenshot shows past the bottom of the note. **U3 did not weaken that check; U3 invalidated its premise:** before U3 the sandbox link sat near the top of a short note and could not be clipped vertically. **This is the only assertion across all six harnesses that tests reachability of a relocated control — the exact question this workstream exists to answer — so a green check named `onScreen` that is false was the worst possible thing for it to be.**

It now measures and RECORDS the vertical truth under names that say what was measured (`horizontallyWithinViewport`, `verticallyWithinViewport`, `withinTheNotesVisibleRegion`, `hitTestable`, plus the note's `scrollTop` / `scrollHeight` / `clientHeight`), takes a screenshot before and after (`04-…`, `04b-…-scrolled-to`), and **asserts the claim that is true instead of forcing the false one green**: horizontally in the viewport as it lies, and after `scrollIntoView` fully in the viewport, inside the note's visible region, and the topmost element at its own centre. **The below-the-fold finding is recorded as `visibleWithoutScrolling: false` and is carried into the open items above, not painted over.**

**2. THE ORDER — Panelizer first.** See the open items above: a decision, taken at review and reversible in one line.

**3. The role gate is now closed at the DOM** (`ui-reorg-u1` step 6b, four roles, order included, plus an explicit `admin.contains(section)` check). The entry above says why the unit tests could never have done this.

**4. The stop count got its hard pin back.** `ui-reorg-u1`'s surviving two-path test asserted `d.stops >= 6`; the retired `region3-baseline` step used to assert exactly its 8 keys, so after that retirement nothing pinned the count. It is now `EXPECTED_VIEW_STOPS = 8`, a named constant checked against both `twoPath.length` and the deduplicated menu label list. The run walked all 8 before and after, so this was a latent floor rather than a live miss.

**5. `smearforn-stage-3`'s `openPanelizer` is symmetric.** Its early-return guard looked for a Scope of work group anywhere in the document while its post-open check insisted on one inside `#settings-note`. Both are scoped now.

## The hidden canvas that never stopped drawing (2026-10-03) — BUILT, branch `frameloop`

**One line of behaviour, two bugs, and the second one was not the one anybody was looking for.** The Project Summary's static 3D rendering is produced by `BuildingSummaryRender`, which mounts a full `Building3DView` inside a react-three-fiber `<Canvas>` parked at `position: fixed; left: -9999px` and grabs one frame as a PNG. `page.tsx` mounts it **unconditionally whenever a footprint exists** — it is not inside a `StickyNote`, so unlike every other heavy surface in this app it is alive for the entire session.

### Bug 1, the one that was reported: the loop never stops

react-three-fiber's default is `frameloop="always"`, which renders for as long as the Canvas is mounted. `grep -rn "frameloop" apps/web/app/` returned **zero occurrences** before this change, so nothing ever told any canvas to stop. The off-screen canvas therefore redrew the whole building at 60fps, forever, for a picture it had already taken.

### Bug 2, found while verifying bug 1, and it is the more dangerous one

The brief for this work stated the current behaviour was *"correct but wasteful — because the canvas always renders, the captured PNG is always current"*, and warned against a naive fix that made it *"cheap but stale"*. **That premise was false. It was already stale, and had been for as long as `CaptureFrame` has existed.**

`CaptureFrame`'s effect was keyed on `[gl, onCapture]`. `gl` is stable for the life of the Canvas, and `onCapture` is `handleCaptureRenderImage` in `page.tsx` — a `useCallback(..., [])`, i.e. a **stable identity for the life of the page**. So the effect ran exactly once per mount, and `BuildingSummaryRender` is never remounted (same position, same type, no `key`; `footprint` going from one building to another does not unmount it). The comment at the `renderImageDataUrl` state said the capture was *"re-captured whenever the callback identity below changes (i.e. whenever the scene inputs do)"*, which is a description of a mechanism that was never there. **The summary image showed the building as of page load.**

Measured on a production build (`next build` + `next start`) of `main` @ `2422fbd`, headless Chrome 154: draw a 55-panel building, open Project Summary, change the wall height, re-open. The summary's own numbers moved — **total weight 5223.0 lb → 8114.3 lb, price $28031.66 → $44651.02**, and the panel fabrication list gained a `Standard 25.5in (4 copies)` page — while the rendering image stayed **byte-identical, SHA-256 `813dfc105388b943` on both sides**. Reproduced in all four "before" harness runs across both panel counts.

### The fix: `frameloop="demand"`, and capture per rendered frame

Two changes, both in `Building3DView.tsx`:

1. `frameloop={captureMode ? "demand" : "always"}` on the `<Canvas>`. In demand mode r3f renders **only** when its reconciler has committed a change to the scene graph.
2. `CaptureFrame` now hangs off `useFrame` instead of a mount-time effect, debounced (`CAPTURE_SETTLE_MS = 300`) and deduped against the last data URL.

**The property that makes this correct is worth stating on its own, because it is the whole argument.** Under `demand`, *"a frame was rendered"* and *"the design changed"* are **the same event**. So the capture needs no dependency list enumerating footprint/slots/heights/beams/headers/roof — it is derived rather than enumerated, and an enumerated list is exactly the thing that goes quietly stale. (That is not a theoretical worry here: the mechanism being replaced went stale because a dependency list of two items was wrong about one of them.)

The dedupe guard is the second half: if a frame renders that happens to draw the same pixels, `onCapture` is not called, so there is no `page.tsx` state update and no re-render. That is what makes a capture → setState → re-render → capture cycle impossible by construction, rather than relying on r3f's commit diffing to not re-invalidate.

### What was rejected, and why

**Mount on demand** — have the Canvas exist only while a capture is needed, or while the Project Summary note is open, then unmount. It removes the cost entirely rather than reducing it, including the per-edit scene-graph reconcile that `demand` keeps. Rejected on three grounds:

- `renderImageDataUrl` is not only the note's image; it is what the **print and PDF-export** paths put on the page. A canvas that mounts only when the note is open means a PDF exported without first opening that note and waiting on it carries a Project Summary with **no rendering at all** — silent content loss in a document that goes to a client. Making that safe means touching the export plumbing in `page.tsx`, which is adjacent to the `page.tsx` restructuring that is explicitly the next piece of work and not this one.
- Mounting a WebGL context and building the entire scene on note-open is a multi-hundred-millisecond first-open stall, which `demand` does not have.
- It needs new `page.tsx` state meaning *"a capture is wanted"*, whose correctness is an **enumerated condition** — the same class of thing that made the capture stale in the first place.

**Honest about what `demand` does NOT remove:** the hidden canvas stays mounted, so r3f still reconciles its scene graph on every change to the design. That cost is real and it is per-edit, not per-frame. It is also precisely what keeps the PNG current, so it is a trade rather than an oversight. Removing it is the mount-on-demand design above, and it should be revisited **with** the `page.tsx` render-cost work rather than before it.

### The measurement

Harness: `apps/web/harness/frameloop-perf/run.mjs`, in the repo like the Smearforn and ui-reorg ones. Production build both sides, headless Chrome 154, `Profiler` domain at a 200µs sampling interval, a **2.5s idle window in plan view with no input at all**. Plan view is the fixture on purpose: the editor's own `Building3DView` is mounted only on the 3D view stop, so in plan view the off-screen summary canvas is the **only** WebGL surface on the page and anything three.js burns is attributable to it by construction. Each figure is the second of two consecutive idle passes (the first headless Chrome launch of a session draws a different footprint than later ones), and each configuration was run twice.

| | panels | idle busy main-thread (of ~2.8s) | WebGL draw calls / idle second | draws / frame | longest idle task |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **before**, 1 storey, 10ft | 55 | **2702.9 ms (97.5%)** / 2559.2 ms (92.9%) | 46,485 / 57,784 | ~775 / ~963 | 313 ms / none ≥50ms |
| **after**, 1 storey, 10ft | 55 | **1.7 ms (0.1%)** / 1.3 ms (0.0%) | **0** / **0** | 0 | none |
| **before**, 2 storeys, 16ft | 110 | **2805.8 ms (100%)** / 2845.4 ms (99.9%) | 70,281 / 58,483 | ~1171 / ~975 | 61 ms / 432 ms |
| **after**, 2 storeys, 16ft | 110 | **1.5 ms (0.0%)** / 0.7 ms (0.0%) | **0** / **0** | 0 | none |

**⚠ Which of these numbers to trust, and which not.** Headless Chrome rasterises WebGL in software (SwiftShader), so the **millisecond** figures on the "before" rows are an upper bound against a real machine with a real GPU — the rasterisation share is pessimistic. What is main-thread *anywhere* is the JavaScript, and the profile says plainly that a lot of it was: the top self-time frames on the before runs are `renderBufferDirect`, `updateMatrixWorld`, `setMaterial`, `setup`, `refreshMaterialUniforms`, `multiplyMatrices`.

**The draw-call count is the figure that carries no caveat at all**, which is why the harness instruments it: `drawElements`/`drawArrays` are patched on both WebGL prototypes before any app script runs, so the count is a direct, hardware-independent statement of whether a render loop is running. ~46,000–70,000 draw calls issued per second while the user did nothing, versus **zero**. A millisecond figure can be argued about; that cannot.

**And note the shape of the "after" column: it is flat, not proportional.** The fix does not make the loop cheaper, it stops the loop, so the after figure is zero at every panel count rather than scaling down from the before figure. That is why two panel counts are enough.

⚠ **Why the two counts are 55 and 110 rather than the ~60 and ~300 the work was briefed with.** The panel count reachable by *drawing* is hard-capped: `FootprintCanvas` fixes the plan canvas at `CANVAS_WIDTH/CANVAS_HEIGHT = 720/480` and converts the drag at a fixed `SCALE_PX_PER_FT = 12`, so the largest footprint a drag can produce is about 59×39ft — **55 ground-floor panels, measured, and a second storey is the only lever that doubles it.** Zooming the plan view out first does **not** help, which was measured rather than assumed: the same 500×340px drag produced **41 panels at zoom 0, 41 at zoom 3 and 41 at zoom 5**. Whether that is intended is not something this pass investigated and it is listed in Open Items as a question, not a finding. A ~300-panel fixture has to come from somewhere other than the drawing gesture.

### Verifying the PNG is still produced and still current

Not asserted — measured, on both sides, in every run. The harness opens the Project Summary note, reads the `src` of the `data:image/png` `<img>` the page is actually showing, SHA-256s it, commits a real wall-height change through the Settings note's own `Wall height` field (typed then Enter, the full `LengthInput` commit gesture, with the committed value read back off the field), re-opens the note and SHA-256s the image again. **Before: identical hash, all four runs. After: different hash, all four runs**, and the after image is also substantially larger (89,710 → 124,018 bytes at 55 panels), consistent with a taller building drawing more geometry. Screenshots of the note either side of the change are checked in under `apps/web/harness/frameloop-perf/screenshots/` and show a short building becoming a tall two-band one.

A separate idle window is measured **after** the edit and the re-capture, and reports **0 draw calls**, which is what proves the canvas goes quiet again rather than being re-armed into a permanent loop by its own capture.

### The canvas audit — every react-three `<Canvas>` in the app

Four files contain a `<Canvas>`. ⚠ **`RoofTrussLayoutView` and `BaleFoundationCrossSectionDiagram` are named on the suspect list but are not WebGL at all — both are SVG** (zero `@react-three/*` imports), so no frameloop applies to them. Mount conditions were read from `page.tsx` and then confirmed in the running app: the harness counts the canvases in the live DOM and identifies the WebGL ones **positively**, by tagging any canvas that asks `getContext` for a `webgl*` context, rather than inferring from position.

| Canvas | Mounted when | Always mounted? | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| `BuildingSummaryRender` → `Building3DView captureMode` | `footprint !== null`, at the top level of the editor — **not inside a `StickyNote`** | **YES** | **The bug.** Fixed: `frameloop="demand"`. |
| `Building3DView` (the editor's own 3D view) | the else-branch of `viewMode === "elevation" ? … : viewMode === "plan" ? … :` — i.e. **only on a 3D view stop** | No | **Correct as-is.** It has `OrbitControls` and a user looking at it; an orbit camera legitimately wants a continuous loop *while being looked at*, and it stops costing anything the moment the user leaves 3D. Deliberately left on `always`. |
| `OctagonRingPreview` | inside `roofToolsControls`, which is `editorTab === "roof" ? (…) : null`, and further gated on `footprint.corners.length === 8` | No | Fine. Visible when mounted; an 8-box scene. |
| `StandardPanel3DView` (9 call sites) | all inside `StickyNote` children | No | Fine. |
| `TruckLoad3DView` | inside the `detail-shipping` `StickyNote` | No | Fine. |

**The `StickyNote` fact the audit rests on, verified rather than assumed:** `StickyNote` does `if (!isOpen) return null`, so a closed section's content is never mounted — the JSX elements are constructed by `page.tsx` but no component below them renders, so no WebGL context is created. Confirmed live: in plan view at both 55 and 110 panels the DOM held **exactly two canvases** — the plan editor's 2D Konva stage (not WebGL) and the summary canvas at `left: -9999px` (WebGL) — with **245–250 DOM nodes**, matching the 240–248 measured independently by the profiler pass.
